summary: Benoist's solution of the period-index problem for function fields of real surfaces (Publ. IHÉS 2019), planned from the pinned libraries. PI.0 builds the real-function-field theory the proof needs and no roadmap owns: orderings with the Harrison topology, real closures at an ordering, signatures, the clopen locus where a Brauer class survives, the Elman–Lam u-invariant, Witt's theorem for real curves, Springer, Amer–Brumer, Albert and Pfister's index-two criterion. PI.1 sets up unramified loci, real evaluation, de Jong's theorem (imported reduction) and the norm bound ind | 2 per. PI.2 is Benoist's Hodge-theoretic proof of de Jong for unramified classes on complex surfaces. PI.3–PI.6 build the ramified double covers, show the pulled-back class is unramified with vanishing topological obstruction, construct a Noether–Lefschetz locus of the expected dimension, control the real locus, and prove the degree-two splitting (Proposition 6.6) under uniform real evaluation, the form the main induction uses. PI.7 proves Theorems 0.3, 0.4, the sufficient half of 0.5, 0.10, 0.12 and 0.13; PI.8 the obstruction (Proposition 7.1, ind = 2 per); PI.9 real Enriques surfaces (Theorem 0.6) and the Puiseux counterexample (Proposition 0.7). Topology comes from AlgebraicTopologyPartII, Hodge theory from HodgeStructuresPartII H.8, period/index arithmetic from SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII, purity from PurityForFlatCohomology, cycle classes from MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles. Gaps: the nonuniform general Propositions 4.4–4.5 and 6.6, de Jong's reduction, the relative pair transport, the inherited Jannsen chase, and five cited classical inputs.

nodes.title: The space of orderings with the Harrison topology
nodes.statement: For a field F, the space of orderings X_F is the set of positive cones P ⊂ F of field orderings, that is the ring preorderings P of F with P ∪ (−P) = F and P ∩ (−P) = {0} (Mathlib's RingPreordering with RingPreordering.IsOrdering). For a ∈ Fˣ write a >_P 0 when a ∈ P, and H(a) = {P ∈ X_F : a >_P 0}. The Harrison topology on X_F is the topology generated by the sets H(a), a ∈ Fˣ. A field embedding ι : F → L induces the restriction map X_L → X_F, Q ↦ ι⁻¹(Q). X_F is empty exactly when F is nonreal, that is when −1 is a sum of squares in F.
hypotheses: F is a field; orderings are positive cones of total orders compatible with the field operations.
The topology is generated by the subbasis H(a), a ∈ Fˣ; complements H(a)ᶜ = H(−a) are again basic.
proofSteps: Take the subtype of RingPreordering F satisfying RingPreordering.IsOrdering; H(a) is the set of P containing a.
The complement of H(a) in X_F is H(−a), because for a ≠ 0 exactly one of a, −a lies in P; so each H(a) is clopen.
Restriction along ι sends an ordering Q of L to ι⁻¹(Q), an ordering of F, and pulls H(a) back to H(ι a); hence it is continuous.

Emptiness: an ordering contains all sums of squares and not −1; conversely if −1 is not a sum of squares, the sums of squares form a proper preordering, contained in an ordering by Zorn (the preordering-extension lemma of upstream RealAlgebraicGeometry Layer 1, which uses Mathlib's RingPreordering API).
acceptance: X_ℝ consists of one point, the cone of nonnegative reals.
X_ℂ is empty, since −1 is a square.
X_{ℚ(√2)} has exactly two points, distinguished by the sign of √2.

nodes.title: Compactness of the Harrison space and inverse limits
nodes.statement: For every field F the space X_F is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected. If F is the directed union of subfields F_i, the restriction maps identify X_F with the inverse limit of the X_{F_i}; consequently, if Z_i ⊂ X_{F_i} are closed subsets with restriction mapping Z_j into Z_i for F_i ⊂ F_j, and the inverse limit of the Z_i is empty, then some Z_i is empty.
hypotheses: F is a field; the F_i form a directed family of subfields with union F.
proofSteps: Embed X_F into the product {±1}^{Fˣ} by P ↦ (sign_P(a))_a; the image is closed, being cut out by the cone axioms, each of which involves finitely many coordinates.
Tychonoff gives compactness; the product is Hausdorff and totally disconnected, and so is the closed subspace.

An ordering of F is the union of its restrictions to the F_i, and compatible orderings of the F_i glue, so X_F → lim X_{F_i} is a continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff spaces, hence a homeomorphism.
An inverse limit of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces is nonempty; so empty limit forces some Z_i to be empty.
acceptance: For F = ℝ(t) the space X_F is infinite and compact.
For the directed union of the finite extensions K_i of a finitely generated K_0 ⊂ K, the limit statement is exactly the Tychonoff step of Benoist p. 96.

sources.match: The space of orderings with the Harrison topology is compact, totally disconnected and Hausdorff; ring maps induce continuous maps of real spectra.

nodes.title: Real closure at a specified ordering
nodes.statement: For a field F and an ordering P ∈ X_F, a real closure of F at P is a field R with IsRealClosed R together with a ring homomorphism ι : F → R making R algebraic over F, such that ι(P) is contained in the set of squares of R (equivalently ι is order-preserving for P and the unique ordering of R). Every pair (F, P) has a real closure. A class β ∈ Br(F) vanishes at P if β becomes trivial in Br(R) for every real closure (R, ι) at P; it vanishes at all real closures if this holds for every P.
hypotheses: F a field, P an ordering of F; R real closed; ι algebraic.
No uniqueness of the real closure is used: the vanishing predicates quantify over all real closures at P.
proofSteps: Existence: convert P into a linear order on F with LinearOrder.mkOfAddGroupCone and IsOrderedRing.mkOfCone, then apply the upstream RealAlgebraicGeometry Layer 1 target exists_realClosure, which gives an algebraic ordered real closure with a strictly monotone embedding.
Strict monotonicity sends P into the nonnegative elements of R, which are the squares of R because R is real closed (IsRealClosed.isSquare_neg_of_not_isSquare).

Brauer groups restrict along ι by TauCeti.BrauerGroup.baseChange; for real closed R, Br(R) has two elements, the trivial class and the quaternion class (−1,−1), because R(i) is algebraically closed and Br(R(i)/R) ≅ Rˣ/(R(i)ˣ norms) = Rˣ/R_{>0}.
acceptance: (ℝ, id) is a real closure of ℝ at its unique ordering.
The real algebraic numbers with the inclusion form a real closure of ℚ at its unique ordering.
ℂ with an embedding of ℝ is not a real closure: it is not real closed.

nodes.title: Signature of a quadratic form at an ordering
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0, q a nondegenerate quadratic form on a finite-dimensional F-vector space and P ∈ X_F. The signature sign_P(q) ∈ ℤ is #{i : a_i >_P 0} − #{i : a_i <_P 0} for any orthogonal diagonalisation q ≅ ⟨a_1, …, a_n⟩. It does not depend on the diagonalisation (Sylvester's law of inertia over an ordered field). The form q has zero total signature if sign_P(q) = 0 for every P ∈ X_F; for nonreal F this condition is empty.
hypotheses: char F = 0 (2 invertible suffices); q nondegenerate on a finite-dimensional space.
Diagonalisations are those of Mathlib's QuadraticForm.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_units_of_nondegenerate'.
proofSteps: Diagonalise q over F (Mathlib, nondegenerate case).
Base change to a real closure (R, ι) at P (PI.0/real-closure-at-ordering): positive diagonal entries become squares, so q_R ≅ ⟨1,…,1,−1,…,−1⟩ with r entries 1 and s entries −1.

Sylvester's law over the ordered field R: r is the largest dimension of a subspace on which q_R is positive definite, so r and s are independent of the diagonalisation; this is the argument of Mathlib's real classification, run over R.

Additivity under orthogonal sums, multiplicativity under tensor products and invariance under isometry follow from diagonal calculus (upstream QuadraticFormInvariants Layers 0–1); local constancy in P holds because each sign_P(a_i) is constant on H(a_i) and on H(−a_i).
acceptance: sign(⟨1,1⟩) = 2 over ℝ.
The hyperbolic plane has signature 0 at every ordering.
Over ℝ(t), ⟨1, −t⟩ has signature 0 at orderings with t > 0 and 2 at orderings with t < 0.

nodes.title: The locus where a Brauer class survives is clopen
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 and β ∈ Br(F). For an ordering P, whether β becomes trivial over a real closure at P does not depend on the real closure, and the set Z(β) = {P ∈ X_F : β does not vanish at P} is clopen in X_F. For a field extension L/F, Z(β_L) is the preimage of Z(β) under restriction X_L → X_F.
hypotheses: char F = 0; β ∈ Br(F) represented by a central simple algebra A of degree d.
proofSteps: Let T_A be the reduced trace form x ↦ Trd(x²) on A, a nondegenerate quadratic form of dimension d² over F.

Over a real closed field R, A_R ≅ M_d(R) or M_{d/2}(ℍ_R); the trace form of M_d(R) has signature d (symmetric minus antisymmetric matrices), and that of ℍ_R is 2⟨1,−1,−1,−1⟩ of signature −2, so the trace form of M_{d/2}(ℍ_R) has signature −d.
Hence β vanishes at P iff sign_P(T_A) = d, a condition independent of the real closure (PI.0/signature-at-ordering).
P ↦ sign_P(T_A) is locally constant, so Z(β) = {P : sign_P(T_A) = −d} is clopen.
Restriction: (T_A)_L = T_{A_L} and a real closure of L at Q is one of F at the restricted ordering when composed with F → L, which gives Z(β_L) = res⁻¹ Z(β).
acceptance: Over ℝ, Z of the quaternion class is the whole one-point space.
For β = (−1, t) over ℝ(t), Z(β) = H(−t), the orderings with t < 0.

nodes.title: The Elman–Lam u-invariant
nodes.statement: For a field F of characteristic 0, u(F) ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞} is the supremum of dim q over nondegenerate anisotropic quadratic forms q over F with zero total signature (sign_P(q) = 0 for every P ∈ X_F); the zero form counts with dimension 0. For nonreal F the signature condition is empty and u(F) is the classical maximal dimension of an anisotropic form. By definition u(F) ≤ n iff every nondegenerate form of dimension > n with zero total signature is isotropic.
hypotheses: char F = 0.
The supremum is taken in ℕ∞; forms with nonzero signature somewhere are not counted.
proofSteps: Define the set of dimensions of anisotropic zero-signature forms and take its supremum in ℕ∞.
The characterisation of u(F) ≤ n is the definition of the supremum; isotropy is the negation of Mathlib's QuadraticMap.Anisotropic.
For nonreal F, HasZeroSignatures holds for every form because X_F is empty (PI.0/ordering-space).

nodes.title: A C₁ field has trivial Brauer group
nodes.statement: If F is a C₁ field (every form of degree d in more than d variables over F has a nontrivial zero), then Br(F) = 0. In particular the function field of an integral curve over an algebraically closed field, and every algebraic extension of it, has trivial Brauer group.
hypotheses: F a field which is C₁ in the sense of QuadraticFormInvariantsPartII:Q2.5/ci.
proofSteps: Let D be a central division algebra of degree d > 1 over F; its reduced norm is a form of degree d in d² > d variables, so it has a nontrivial zero by C₁.
A nonzero element of D with reduced norm 0 is not invertible, contradicting that D is a division algebra; so every central division algebra over F is F itself.
Every Brauer class has a central division representative (TauCeti.BrauerGroup.exists_eq_mk_centralDivisionRing), so Br(F) = 0.
Curve function fields over algebraically closed fields are C₁ by Tsen–Lang (QuadraticFormInvariantsPartII:Q2.5/transcendental-ci), and algebraic extensions of C₁ fields are C₁ (Q2.5/algebraic-ci).

nodes.title: Witt's theorem on Brauer classes of real curves
nodes.statement: Let C be a smooth integral curve over ℝ with function field F = ℝ(C). (a) A class β ∈ Br(F) that vanishes at every real closure of F is zero. (b) If β is unramified at the points of a Euclidean-dense subset W of C(ℝ) and β(x) = 0 ∈ Br(ℝ) for x ∈ W, then β vanishes at every real closure, hence β = 0; the class may be ramified elsewhere. (c) If C(ℝ) = ∅, then F is nonreal and Br(F) = 0.
hypotheses: C smooth, integral, of finite type and separated over ℝ; ramification of β at finitely many points is allowed.
W ⊂ C(ℝ) dense for the Euclidean topology; evaluation at x ∈ W uses the unramified locus of PI.1/unramified-locus.
proofSteps: Tsen: Br(ℂ(C)) = 0 (PI.0/ci-brauer-vanishing; SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.16), so β is split by the quadratic extension F(i)/F and equals the quaternion class (−1, f) for some f ∈ Fˣ (cyclic algebras; upstream QuadraticFormInvariants Layers 2 and 5).
At an ordering P, β vanishes over the real closure iff f >_P 0 (PI.0/real-closure-at-ordering, Br(R) = {0, (−1,−1)}).
(a) If f is positive at every ordering, the norm form ⟨1, 1, −f, −f⟩ of (−1, f) has zero total signature; by PI.0/curve-u-bound it is isotropic, so (−1, f) splits.

(b) Every ordering of F is centred at a real point of the smooth completion of C and is determined by a half-branch there; the sign of f at the ordering is its sign on that half-branch near the centre. Since W is dense, f > 0 near every real point along every half-branch, so f >_P 0 for every P and (a) applies.
(c) If C(ℝ) = ∅, the smooth completion has no real points outside a finite set, so there are no half-branches and no orderings: F is nonreal, and (a) holds vacuously for every β.
acceptance: Br(ℝ(C)) = 0 for the conic C : x² + y² = −1.
Over ℝ(t), the class (−1, t) is nonzero: it does not vanish at the orderings with t < 0, matching (a).
Over ℝ(t), the class (−1, 1 + t²) is zero, consistent with (b): it evaluates to 0 at every real point.

nodes.title: Springer's theorem for complete discretely valued fields
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field with residue field k of characteristic ≠ 2 and uniformizer π. A diagonal form q = ⟨u_1, …, u_r⟩ ⊥ π⟨v_1, …, v_s⟩ with units u_i, v_j is anisotropic over K iff both residue forms ⟨ū_1, …, ū_r⟩ and ⟨v̄_1, …, v̄_s⟩ are anisotropic over k. Applied twice, the form ⟨1, y₁, −y₂, −y₁y₂⟩ is anisotropic over the iterated Laurent series field ℂ((y₁))((y₂)).
hypotheses: K complete for a discrete valuation; char k ≠ 2; all u_i, v_j units.
proofSteps: If a residue form is isotropic, Hensel's lemma (completeness, char k ≠ 2) lifts a nonsingular zero to a zero of the corresponding unit form, so q is isotropic.

Conversely, if q(x) = 0 with x primitive, compare valuations: the unit part and the π-part cannot cancel unless both reductions have a nontrivial zero; this is the anisotropy of reductions of anisotropic unimodular forms over a complete DVR.
The Witt-ring form: the two residue homomorphisms give a split exact sequence identifying W(K) with W(k) ⊕ W(k).
For ℂ((y₁))((y₂)): write ⟨1, y₁⟩ ⊥ (−y₂)⟨1, y₁⟩; both residue forms are ⟨1, y₁⟩ up to sign over ℂ((y₁)), which is anisotropic by the same theorem since ⟨1⟩ is anisotropic over ℂ.

nodes.title: The Amer–Brumer theorem
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic ≠ 2 and φ, ψ quadratic forms on the same finite-dimensional F-vector space V. Then φ and ψ have a common nonzero isotropic vector in V iff the form φ + tψ on V ⊗ F(t) over the rational function field F(t) is isotropic.
hypotheses: char F ≠ 2 (EKM proves it in all characteristics); φ, ψ on the same space V.
proofSteps: A common zero v gives the constant vector v with (φ + tψ)(v) = 0.

Conversely take a nonzero polynomial vector v(t) ∈ V[t] with (φ + tψ)(v) = 0 of minimal degree; a degree-reduction argument (EKM Theorem 17.14) shows deg v = 0, and then the coefficients of 1 and t give φ(v) = ψ(v) = 0.

Over ℝ, φ = ⟨1, 1⟩ and ψ = ⟨1, −1⟩ have no common nonzero zero, and φ + tψ = ⟨1 + t, 1 − t⟩ is anisotropic over ℝ(t), since −(1 + t)/(1 − t) is not a square there.

nodes.title: Albert's isotropy criterion for six-dimensional forms
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic ≠ 2 and φ a nondegenerate quadratic form of dimension 6 and trivial discriminant (an Albert form). Its Clifford invariant c(φ) ∈ Br(F)[2] is the class of a central simple algebra of degree 4, and φ is isotropic iff the index of c(φ) is at most 2.
hypotheses: char F ≠ 2; dim φ = 6; signed discriminant of φ trivial.
proofSteps: Scaling by d = −det⟨x₁,x₂,x₃⟩ puts φ = ⟨x₁,…,x₆⟩ of trivial discriminant into the normal form dφ ≅ ⟨a, b, −ab, −c, −d, cd⟩ (diagonal calculus, upstream QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 0); similarity preserves isotropy and the Clifford invariant of an even-dimensional form of trivial discriminant.
For this normal form the even Clifford algebra is A × A with A = (a, b) ⊗ (c, d), so c(φ) = [A] (upstream QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 5, Clifford invariant).

nodes.title: Pfister's criterion: index two implies u ≤ 4
nodes.statement: Let K be a field extension of ℝ of transcendence degree 2. If every nonzero class α ∈ Br(K)[2] that vanishes at all real closures of K has index 2, then u(K) ≤ 4 in the Elman–Lam sense. (Pfister proves the equivalence; only this direction is a target.)

proofSteps: By PI.0/elman-lam-c2-bound, u(K) ∈ {0,1,2,4,6}; suppose u(K) = 6 and take an anisotropic Albert form φ with zero total signature.

At every ordering P, φ_R over a real closure R at P is six-dimensional of signature 0, hence hyperbolic; so c(φ)_R = c(φ_R) = 0 (Clifford invariant commutes with base change). Thus c(φ) vanishes at all real closures.
By hypothesis c(φ) has index ≤ 2 (index 1 if c(φ) = 0), so φ is isotropic by PI.0/albert-isotropy, a contradiction. Hence u(K) ≤ 4.

nodes.title: Unramified locus of a Brauer class
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth integral variety over a field k of characteristic 0, with Br(X) = H²_ét(X, 𝔾_m) ⊂ Br(k(X)). For α ∈ Br(k(X)) only finitely many prime divisors Γ ⊂ X have nonzero residue res_Γ(α) ∈ H¹(k(Γ), ℚ/ℤ); their union is the ramification divisor of α, and its complement U_α is the largest open subset U ⊂ X with α ∈ Br(U) ⊂ Br(k(X)). For a proper surface S over ℝ and α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)), U_α is a dense open of S whose complement is a curve.

nodes.title: De Jong's period-index theorem in characteristic zero
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 and S a connected smooth projective surface over k. For every α ∈ Br(k(S)), ind(α) = per(α).

nodes.statement: Let R be a real closed field and F the function field of an integral surface over R. For α ∈ Br(F) of period n, ind(α) divides 2n; hence ind(α) ∈ {n, 2n}, and ind(α) = n if n is odd.

proofSteps: If √−1 ∈ F, F is the function field of a surface over the algebraically closed field R(√−1), and PI.1/de-jong-period-index gives ind = per.
Otherwise L = F(√−1) is the function field of a surface over R(√−1); by de Jong, ind(α_L) = per(α_L), which divides n.
Reverse index divisibility (SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII:SA.0/index-divides-degree-index): ind(α) divides [L : F]·ind(α_L) = 2 ind(α_L), which divides 2n.
Period divides index and both have the same prime divisors (SA.1), so ind(α) ∈ {n, 2n}, and for odd n the factor 2 is excluded.
acceptance: For Albert's class (x, x) + (y, xy) over ℝ(x, y), the period is 2 and the index is 4 = 2n.
Every class of odd period over ℝ(S) has index equal to its period.

sources.match: De Jong's theorem and a norm argument give ind ∈ {per, 2 per}; odd period gives equality.

nodes.title: Removing finitely many points and extending line bundles
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth integral surface over ℝ and V ⊂ S a dense open. Every line bundle on V extends to S (Pic(S) → Pic(V) is onto). If Z ⊂ S is finite and Σ ⊂ S(ℝ) is a union of connected components, restriction H¹(Σ, 𝔽₂) → H¹(Σ ∖ Z, 𝔽₂) is injective. These are the extension and injectivity steps used to pass from the finite-flat open U₀ to U.
hypotheses: S smooth, so Weil and Cartier divisors agree; Σ a surface (two-dimensional manifold) and Z finite.
proofSteps: A line bundle on V is O_V(D) for a Weil divisor D on V; its closure in S is a Weil divisor, Cartier since S is smooth, restricting to D.

Σ ∖ Z ⊂ Σ: removing points from a surface does not change H¹ except through H¹ classes supported near the points, and the long exact sequence of the pair with H¹ of a punctured disc neighbourhood shows the restriction is injective (excision gives H¹(Σ, Σ ∖ Z) = ⊕ H¹(D, D ∖ {pt}) = 0).
acceptance: For Σ = S² and Z one point, H¹(S²) = 0 → H¹(ℝ²) = 0 is injective.
For Σ a torus and Z a point, H¹ is unchanged.

nodes.title: Hypersurfaces in P¹ × S of degree divisible by the period
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective complex surface, α ∈ Br(S) of period n, and A a very ample line bundle with A² > A·K_S. Put X = ℙ¹ × S and H = pr₁*O(1) ⊗ pr₂*A, very ample on X; then H²·K_X = 2(A·K_S − A²) < 0. For d ≥ 1 let B_d ⊂ |dnH| be the Zariski-open locus of smooth surfaces and T → B_d the universal family; each fibre T_b comes with p_b : T_b → S, generically finite of degree dn, and its class in H²(X(ℂ), ℤ) is dn·c₁(H), divisible by n.
hypotheses: S connected smooth projective over ℂ; A very ample with A² > A·K_S; d ≥ 1.
proofSteps: K_X = pr₁*K_{ℙ¹} + pr₂*K_S; expand H²·K_X with h² = 0 on ℙ¹ and A²·K_S = 0 on the surface S to get 2(A·K_S − A²).

H is very ample (Segre embedding of very ample bundles; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1/ample-powers-and-fixed-twists for its powers), and Bertini (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.13) makes the smooth members of |dnH| a dense Zariski open B_d; the universal family is the incidence divisor in B_d × X.
The degree of p_b is the intersection of T_b with a fibre ℙ¹ × {s}, namely dn.
acceptance: For S = ℙ² and A = O(1), A² = 1 > −3 = A·K_S.
For a quintic surface in ℙ³ with A = O(1), A² = 5 = A·K_S, so A = O(1) is excluded and A = O(2) is required.

nodes.title: The pulled-back class has no topological obstruction
nodes.statement: In PI.2/complex-hypersurface-family, for every b ∈ B_d(ℂ), the image τ of p_b*α ∈ Br(T_b)[n] in H³(T_b(ℂ), ℤ)[n] under the complex topological Brauer sequence 0 → H²(ℤ)/⟨n, Pic⟩ → Br[n] → H³(ℤ)[n] → 0 vanishes.
hypotheses: The setting of PI.2/complex-hypersurface-family.
proofSteps: With i : T_b ↪ X, the composite i_*i* is cup product with cl(T_b) = dn c₁(H) (projection formula), hence kills the n-torsion class pr₂*τ_S.
i_* : H³(T_b, ℤ) → H⁵(X, ℤ) is an isomorphism by integral weak Lefschetz (HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h3).
τ = p_b*τ_S = i*pr₂*τ_S maps to zero under the isomorphism i_*, so τ = 0.
acceptance: If H³(S(ℂ), ℤ) has no torsion (S = ℙ²), τ_S = 0 already.

nodes.title: Compatible integral lift and pushforward adjustment
nodes.statement: In PI.2/complex-hypersurface-family fix a Kummer lift α̃ ∈ H²(S(ℂ), ℤ/n) of α. Choose β ∈ H²(T_b(ℂ), ℤ) whose reduction modulo n is exactly p_b*α̃; such β exists because the Bockstein of p_b*α̃ is τ = 0. Then p_{b*}β is divisible by n, and there is γ ∈ H²(T_b(ℂ), ℤ) with p_{b*}(β − nγ) = 0. The class β − nγ lies in H²(T_b, ℤ)_S = ker p_{b*} and still induces p_b*α in Br(T_b).
hypotheses: The setting of PI.2/complex-hypersurface-family; the compatibility β mod n = p_b*α̃ is imposed (an arbitrary integral lift of p_b*α in the Brauer sequence is not enough).
proofSteps: By PI.2/complex-obstruction-vanishes the integral Bockstein of p_b*α̃ vanishes, so it lifts to β ∈ H²(T_b, ℤ).
p_{b*}β reduces to p_{b*}p_b*α̃ = dn·α̃ = 0 modulo n, so p_{b*}β = nε for some ε ∈ H²(S, ℤ).
H²(T_b, ℤ) → H⁴(X, ℤ) is onto (HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/ordinary-integral-lefschetz-h2) and H⁴(ℙ¹ × S, ℤ) → H²(S, ℤ) is onto by the Künneth formula, so ε = p_{b*}γ for some γ.
β − nγ reduces to p_b*α̃ modulo n, so it still induces p_b*α.
acceptance: For α = 0 and α̃ = 0 one may take β = γ = 0.
Replacing β by β + cl(L) for a line bundle L on T_b keeps the Brauer class but can destroy n-divisibility of p_{b*}β.

nodes.title: Dense splitting hypersurfaces
nodes.statement: In PI.2/complex-hypersurface-family, for all sufficiently large d the points b ∈ B_d(ℂ) with p_b*α = 0 ∈ Br(T_b) are dense in B_d(ℂ) for the Euclidean topology.
hypotheses: d large enough for Voisin's theorem (HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/voisin-product-surface).
Transport over contractible opens uses ordinary Ehresmann; the compatible lift is transported as the restriction of the family class pulled back from S, so its reduction stays p_x*α̃.
proofSteps: Fix a nonempty Euclidean open W ⊂ B_d(ℂ); it meets Voisin's Zariski open V; take b ∈ V ∩ W and a contractible neighbourhood Λ ⊂ V ∩ W.
PI.2/compatible-complex-lift gives β − nγ in H²(T_b, ℤ)_S; its image in H²(T_b, ℝ)_S is a lattice coset point modulo n·(lattice).
Voisin's open cone Ω ⊂ H²(T_b, ℝ)_S (H.8/voisin-kernel-cone) meets the coset β − nγ + n·H²(T_b, ℤ)_S (H.8/full-lattice-coset-cone): choose δ with β − nγ − nδ ∈ Ω.

Ehresmann transport over the contractible Λ (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.16/equivariant-ehresmann with trivial involution) identifies the cohomology of the fibres; some x ∈ Λ makes β − nγ − nδ of type (1,1) on T_x; integral Lefschetz (1,1) (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.7/tate-and-hodge-known-cases, entry H1) writes it as c₁ of a line bundle.
The transported β still reduces to p_x*α̃, so in the topological Brauer sequence p_x*α = 0 ∈ Br(T_x).
acceptance: For α = 0 every b qualifies.

nodes.title: Unramified period equals index on complex surfaces
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℂ and α ∈ Br(S) ⊂ Br(ℂ(S)). Then ind(α) = per(α).
hypotheses: S connected smooth projective over ℂ; α unramified on S.
proofSteps: Apply PI.2/dense-splitting-hypersurfaces with two consecutive large integers d, d + 1: there are smooth T ∈ |dnH| and T′ ∈ |(d+1)nH| on which α vanishes.
Their function fields are splitting fields of α of degrees dn and (d+1)n over ℂ(S), so ind(α) divides both (SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII:SA.0/index-divides-splitting-degree), hence divides n.
per(α) divides ind(α) (SA.1/period-divides-index), so ind(α) = n.
acceptance: For S an Enriques surface over ℂ and α the nonzero class of Br(S) ≅ ℤ/2, ind(α) = 2.

nodes.title: The finite double cover branched along R ∪ D
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth surface over a field of characteristic 0, R ⊂ S an SNC divisor with equation r ∈ H⁰(S, O(R)), L a line bundle and s ∈ H⁰(S, L²(R)) with smooth zero divisor D meeting R transversally and avoiding Sing R. Put M = L(R) and b = rs ∈ H⁰(S, M²). The finite model is C = Spec_S(O_S ⊕ M⁻¹), with multiplication M⁻¹ ⊗ M⁻¹ → O_S given by b. It is finite locally free of rank 2, locally z² = rs, étale exactly over S ∖ (R ∪ D), normal, with ordinary double points exactly over Sing(R ∪ D); it carries the involution z ↦ −z with invariant subring O_S.
hypotheses: char 0; R SNC; D smooth, transverse to R, disjoint from Sing R.
If R ∪ D = ∅ the cover is étale and may be disconnected; normality does not assert integrality.
proofSteps: Locally, with M⁻¹ trivialised by z, the algebra is O_S[z]/(z² − b): Mathlib's QuadraticAlgebra O b 0, finite free of rank 2 with basis 1, z.
The discriminant is 4b, so the cover is étale exactly where rs is a unit, that is off R ∪ D.

Normality by Serre's criterion: a hypersurface in a smooth threefold is Cohen–Macaulay, hence S2 (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/ci-cohen-macaulay); it is regular in codimension one because rs vanishes to order 1 along each component of R ∪ D.
At a point of Sing(R ∪ D), local coordinates make b = xy and z² = xy is an ordinary double point; elsewhere on R ∪ D, b is a coordinate and the cover is smooth.
acceptance: S = 𝔸², R = {x = 0}, D = {y = 0}: C = Spec k[x, y, z]/(z² − xy), an A₁ singularity at the origin.
R = D = ∅ and b = 1: C = S ⊔ S.

nodes.title: The incidence model and its resolution
nodes.statement: In PI.3/branch-cover-finite-model, let X̄ = ℙ_S(O ⊕ L) with tautological sections v ∈ H⁰(O(1)) and w ∈ H⁰(O(1) ⊗ f*L⁻¹), and T̄ = {rv² = sw²} ⊂ X̄ with projection p̄ : T̄ → S. There is a proper morphism h : T̄ → C, given by z = r v/w where w ≠ 0 and z = s w/v where v ≠ 0, which is an isomorphism away from R ∩ D. The singular points of T̄ are exactly the points over Sing R with w = 0 (that is [v : w] = [1 : 0]), ordinary double points whose position in X̄ does not depend on s. T is the blow-up of T̄ at these points, p : T → S is proper and generically of degree 2, and blowing up X̄ at the same fixed points gives a smooth projective threefold X in which the T for s ∈ B form a smooth family π : 𝒯 → B ⊂ B × X. The map p is not finite: its fibres over R ∩ D and over Sing R are ℙ¹.
hypotheses: B ⊂ H⁰(S, L²(R)) the open set of sections with D smooth, transverse to R and disjoint from Sing R.
The fixed singular centres are where w vanishes (the published text says v; see RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E18).
proofSteps: On w ≠ 0 write t = v/w, so T̄ is r t² = s; then z = r t satisfies z² = r²t² = rs. On v ≠ 0 write u = w/v, so r = s u², and z = s u satisfies z² = rs. On v, w ≠ 0 both give z = r v/w = s w/v, so h is well defined.
Away from R ∩ D one of r, s is a unit locally and h is an isomorphism; over R ∩ D the fibre of T̄ is the whole ℙ¹ (PI.3/incidence-local-resolution).

Jacobian criterion: over Sing R (where s is a unit and r = xy) the only singular point of the fibre is w = 0, an ordinary double point; elsewhere T̄ is smooth. The point w = 0 over Sing R is the same for every s.

Blow up these finitely many fixed points of X̄ to get X; strict transforms of the T̄ are the resolved T and form a smooth family over B (blow-ups and blow-up strict transforms: upstream StableReduction Layer 4, as re-exported by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/strict-transform and §4.11).
acceptance: If R ∩ D = ∅ and R is smooth, T̄ = C is finite over S and T = T̄.
Over a node of R, T has a single exceptional ℙ¹, mapping to the node.

nodes.title: Local structure and Stein factorisation of the incidence model
nodes.statement: At a point of R ∩ D the surface T̄ is smooth and h : T̄ → C is the minimal resolution of the node z² = rs, with exceptional ℙ¹ of self-intersection −2 (equivalently the blow-up of the ideal (r, z)). The resolved cover factors as T → C → S, both T → C and T̄ → C satisfy h_*O = O_C, R^i h_*O = 0 for i > 0 and have geometrically connected fibres, so C = Spec_S(p_*O_T) and p_*O_T = O_S ⊕ L⁻¹(−R) compatibly with the involution.
hypotheses: The setting of PI.3/incidence-double-cover.
proofSteps: Charts at a crossing: s = r x², z = r x and r = s y², z = s y with y = x⁻¹; both are affine planes, so T̄ is smooth there, and the exceptional curve is ℙ¹ with normal bundle O(−2).

The Čech computation on the two charts gives Γ(O) = k[r, rx, rx²] ≅ k[r, z, s]/(z² − rs) and vanishing higher cohomology, hence h_*O = O_C and R^i h_*O = 0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.2 Čech comparison).

Over Sing R the blow-up of the ordinary double point has the same two properties (rational singularity), and h is proper birational onto the normal C, so h_*O = O_C (proper birational maps to normal schemes; SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.9 Stein factorisation).
Hence p_*O_T = (C → S)_*O_C = O_S ⊕ M⁻¹ with M = L(R), and the involution acts by +1 and −1 on the two summands.
acceptance: The exceptional curve over a crossing has self-intersection −2 on T.

nodes.title: Pushforward on the complex double cover
nodes.statement: If L(R) is ample, then p_* : H^i(T(ℂ), ℤ) → H^i(S(ℂ), ℤ) is an isomorphism for i ≥ 3 and surjective for i = 2.
hypotheses: L(R) ample (Assumption 3.1), so O_S(Δ) ≅ L²(2R) is ample and S*, T* are affine.
proofSteps: S* and its finite étale cover T* are smooth affine surfaces, so their integral cohomology vanishes in degrees ≥ 3 (HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/affine-integral-vanishing); the sign sequence then kills H^i(S*, Z̃) for i ≥ 3.
The triangle Rj₀_*Z̃ → p_*ℤ → ℤ on S₀(ℂ) (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.14/ramified-triangle) gives p_* : H^i(T₀) ≅ H^i(S₀) for i ≥ 3 and onto for i = 2.
Compare the long exact sequences with supports along E ⊂ T and P ⊂ S; p_* : H^j(E) → H^{j−2}(P) is an isomorphism for j ≥ 1 because E is a union of ℙ¹'s over P, and the five lemma concludes.
acceptance: The connected components of T(ℂ) and S(ℂ) correspond (i = 4).

sources.match: Under L(R) ample, p_* is an isomorphism in degrees ≥ 3 and onto in degree 2, by Andreotti–Frankel, the triangle (3.2) and a diagram chase with supports.

nodes.title: Image of the equivariant pushforward
nodes.statement: Let S be defined over ℝ and L(R) ample. Put I = im(p_* : H¹(T(ℝ), 𝔽₂) → H¹(S(ℝ), 𝔽₂)). For every i ≥ 2 the image of p_* : H^i_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(i−1)) → H^i_G(S(ℂ), ℤ(i−1)) is exactly {ξ : [ξ]₁ ∈ I}.
hypotheses: L(R) ample; real components [ξ]₁ as in AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.7/fixed-integral.
proofSteps: For i ≥ 5, restriction to the real locus is an isomorphism (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.6/free-descent, i > 2·dim) and the canonical decomposition identifies both groups with H¹ of the real loci; pushforward acts on real coordinates by the real Gysin map (AT2.9/real-coordinate-maps, AT2.8/equivariant-gysin).

Descending induction: the real–complex exact sequences (AT2.7/sign-class) for T and S, connected by pushforwards, with PI.3/complex-pushforward-iso on the ordinary terms and the induction hypothesis in degree i + 1, identify the image with {ξ : [ξ ∪ ω]₁ ∈ I}.
[ξ ∪ ω]₁ = [ξ]₁ (invariance of integral components under ω, AT2.7/fixed-integral).
acceptance: If T(ℝ) → S(ℝ) is onto in H¹, every class is a pushforward for i ≥ 2.

sources.match: Real substitute for weak Lefschetz: the image of the equivariant pushforward is cut out by the first real component lying in I, by descending induction through real–complex sequences.

nodes.title: Hypotheses on a double cover killing a period-two class
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ, α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)) of period 2 whose ramification divisor R is SNC, U = S ∖ R, Θ = Θ(α) ⊂ U(ℝ), and Ψ ⊂ U(ℝ) a subset open and closed in S(ℝ) with Θ ⊂ Ψ. For a double cover p : T → S of PI.3/incidence-double-cover ramified over R ∪ D, Assumption 4.1 is: (i) p(T(ℝ)) ∩ Ψ = ∅; (ii) the kernel of H¹(S(ℝ), 𝔽₂) → H¹(Ψ, 𝔽₂) is generated by p_*H¹(T(ℝ), 𝔽₂) and the Borel–Haefliger classes cl_R(Γ) of curves Γ ⊂ S with Γ(ℝ) ∩ Ψ = ∅; (iii) p_* : H²(T(ℝ), 𝔽₂) → H²(S(ℝ), 𝔽₂) is injective. Since Δ(ℝ) ⊂ p(T(ℝ)), (i) forces Ψ ⊂ S*(ℝ).
hypotheses: Cohomology of real loci with 𝔽₂ coefficients; cl_R is the Borel–Haefliger class of MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2.
proofSteps: (i)–(iii) are conditions on the real topology of the cover; their consequences are proved in PI.4 and their verification in PI.6/topology-to-cover-hypotheses.
Over a point of Δ(ℝ) the fibre of p has a real point (the ramification point or a real ℙ¹), so Δ(ℝ) ⊂ p(T(ℝ)) and (i) gives Ψ ∩ Δ(ℝ) = ∅.
acceptance: If S(ℝ) = ∅, then Ψ = ∅ and (i)–(iii) hold for every cover.
If D(ℝ) meets Ψ, (i) fails.

nodes.title: The pulled-back class is unramified
nodes.statement: Under Assumption 4.1, α_{ℝ(T)} ∈ Br(T)[2] ⊂ Br(ℝ(T))[2].
hypotheses: Assumption 4.1 (PI.4/brauer-cover-hypotheses).
proofSteps: Residues vanish along integral curves of T not lying over R, because α is unramified on U and pullback preserves this.

Along a curve dominating a component of R, the ramification index is 2 and the residue of the restriction is the ramification index times the restricted residue (residues along a finite extension of DVRs; requested from PurityForFlatCohomology:PF.6), which kills a class of period 2.

The remaining curves Γ are ℙ¹'s contracted by p: the exceptional curves over Sing R and the ℙ¹ fibres over R ∩ D of the incidence model (both kinds must be treated). The ramification locus of α_{ℝ(T)} is then smooth, so by the Gersten complex res_Γ(α) ∈ H¹(ℝ(Γ), ℤ/2) is unramified on Γ.

If Γ ≅ ℙ¹_ℂ, H¹_ét(Γ, ℤ/2) = 0. If Γ ≅ ℙ¹_ℝ, it suffices to show res_Γ(α)|_x = 0 at one x ∈ Γ(ℝ): choose a curve Γ′ through x transverse to Γ and meeting T_U; at general real points y of Γ′, p(y) ∉ Ψ ⊃ Θ by (i), so (p*α)_y = 0, and Witt's theorem (PI.0/witt-real-curve (b), which allows ramification of the class on Γ′) gives p*α|_{ℝ(Γ′)} = 0, so its residue at x, which is res_Γ(α)|_x, vanishes.
All residues along curves of T vanish, so α_{ℝ(T)} ∈ Br(T) by purity for the regular surface T (PurityForFlatCohomology:PF.6/brauer-purity-regular and the DVR residue sequence).
acceptance: If R = ∅ the statement is that α_{ℝ(T)} is unramified on T, which is immediate.

sources.match: α_{ℝ(T)} is unramified: residues along curves over R vanish by ramification index 2; on exceptional curves by Gersten and Witt's theorem along a transverse curve.

nodes.title: The topological obstruction is killed by ω
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1, let τ ∈ H³_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1))[2] be the image of α_{ℝ(T)} ∈ Br(T)[2] in the real topological Brauer sequence 0 → H²_G(ℤ(1))/⟨2, Pic⟩ → Br[2] → H³_G(ℤ(1))[2] → 0. Then τ ∪ ω = 0 in H⁴_G(T(ℂ), ℤ).
hypotheses: Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1; S connected.
proofSteps: The pushforward square from Br(T)[2] → H³_G(T, ℤ(1)) → H⁴_G(T, ℤ) → H⁰ ⊕ H²(T(ℝ)) to the same row for S commutes (equivariant Gysin compatibility).
p_*(α_T) = 2α = 0, so p_*[τ ∪ ω]₂ = 0; by (iii) [τ ∪ ω]₂ = 0. By (i), α evaluates to 0 at p(x) for x ∈ T(ℝ), so [τ ∪ ω]₀ = 0.

The norm sequence H⁴(T(ℂ), ℤ) → H⁴_G(T(ℂ), ℤ) → H⁰ ⊕ H²(T(ℝ)) is exact: the kernel of ∪ω is the norm image (real–complex sequence, AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.7/sign-class), restriction H⁵_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1)) → H⁵_G(T(ℝ), ℤ(1)) is an isomorphism above twice the dimension (AT2.6/free-descent), and the real components of ξ ∪ ω are those of ξ (AT2.7/fixed-integral). So τ ∪ ω = N(c) for some c; T(ℂ) has one component or two exchanged by conjugation (PI.3/complex-pushforward-iso in degree 4), so τ ∪ ω = m·cl(y + σy) for a point y.
Pushing forward to H⁴(S(ℂ), ℤ) kills τ ∪ ω, so m·cl(p(y) + p(σy)) = 0, forcing m = 0.
acceptance: If T(ℝ) = ∅ then the real components vanish trivially and only the norm argument is needed.

sources.match: τ ∪ ω = 0, from the pushforward diagram (4.1), Assumption 4.1 (i) and (iii), the norm sequence of BW1 Lemma 2.11(ii) and degrees of zero-cycles.

nodes.title: The boundary component under constant real evaluation
nodes.statement: In the setting of PI.4/brauer-cover-hypotheses let α̃ ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), 𝔽₂) lift α, with components a₀ = [α̃]₀, a₁ = [α̃]₁ on Ψ, and let ζ = ∂(α̃|_{S*}) ∈ H³_G(S*(ℂ), Z̃(1)) for the boundary of 0 → Z̃(1) → Z̃(1) → 𝔽₂ → 0, and e ∈ H¹_G(S*(ℂ), 𝔽₂) the class of the double cover. If a₁|_Ψ = 0 and a₀|_Ψ is a constant t ∈ 𝔽₂, then [ζ]₁|_Ψ = t·[e]₁|_Ψ, which equals t·cl_R(φ)|_Ψ for any φ ∈ Pic(S) extending the 2-torsion line bundle υ(e) on S*.
hypotheses: Ψ ⊂ S*(ℝ) (consequence of Assumption 4.1 (i)); on Ψ conjugation acts by −1 on Z̃, so the relevant coefficient twist has +1 stalks.
proofSteps: The boundary for the twisted sequence is the twisted Bockstein: Bockstein plus cup with e + ω (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.14/double-cover-extension, AT2.7/twisted-bockstein).
On Ψ, [e + ω]₀ = 1 + 1 = 0 and [e + ω]₁ = [e]₁, so in canonical components (a₀, a₁, a₂) ↦ (0, a₁ + a₀·[e]₁, β(a₁) + a₁·[e]₁) (cup-product convolution, AT2.7/fixed-mod-two).
With a₁ = 0 and a₀ = t this gives [ζ]₁ = t·[e]₁ on Ψ.
Lemma 2.1 of the source (cl_R(υ(e)) = [e]₁; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2) and surjectivity of Pic(S) → Pic(S*) give φ.
acceptance: For t = 0 (the case 4 | n in the induction) [ζ]₁|_Ψ = 0 and no Picard correction is needed.
For t = 1 this recovers the printed formula [ζ]₁ = [e]₁ of the source.

sources.match: Computation of the diagonal boundary in canonical decompositions; the printed conclusion [ζ]₁ = [e]₁ uses a₀ = 1 on Ψ (see RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E3).
The real class of the 2-torsion line bundle of a double-cover class is its degree-one component.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the topological obstruction for uniform evaluation
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1, suppose α has a Kummer lift α̃ ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), 𝔽₂) with [α̃]₁|_Ψ = 0 and [α̃]₀|_Ψ constant equal to t ∈ 𝔽₂. Then the obstruction τ of PI.4/obstruction-cup-omega vanishes, so α_{ℝ(T)} lifts to a class β ∈ H²_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1)).
hypotheses: The uniform-evaluation hypothesis on Ψ; this is the restricted form of the source's Proposition 4.4 that the main induction uses.
The homological comparison (4.5) is AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.16/double-cover-diagram, whose signed contract is that packet's gap (extraction gap G10).
proofSteps: By PI.4/obstruction-cup-omega and the real–complex sequence, τ = N(γ) with γ ∈ H³(T(ℂ), ℤ); p_*γ lifts to δ ∈ H³_G(S(ℂ), ℤ).

Claim: after replacing δ by δ − ξ ∪ ω for some ξ ∈ H²_G(S(ℂ), ℤ(1)), [δ]₁|_Ψ = 0. The double-cover chase comparison (AT2.16/double-cover-diagram) gives η₀ on S₀ with g(δ|_{S₀}) + ζ ∪ ω = g(η₀ ∪ ω); extend η₀ to S by purity and replace δ by δ − (η + t·cl(φ)) ∪ ω, with φ from PI.4/uniform-first-component.
Restricting to Ψ in canonical components, [g(δ)]₁ = [δ]₁, [g(cl(φ) ∪ ω)]₁ = cl_R(φ) = [e]₁ and [ζ ∪ ω]₁ = [ζ]₁ = t[e]₁, so the relation gives [δ]₁|_Ψ = 0.

By Assumption 4.1 (ii) there is θ ∈ Pic(S) with [δ]₁ − cl_R(θ) ∈ I, and by PI.3/equivariant-pushforward-image δ = p_*ε + cl(θ) ∪ ω; since p_* is an isomorphism on H³ (PI.3/complex-pushforward-iso), the diagram chase gives τ = 0.
acceptance: For S(ℝ) = ∅ the hypotheses are empty and τ = 0 for every cover satisfying Assumption 3.1.

sources.match: τ = 0 when a lift with vanishing first component on Ψ exists, by the chase (4.2)–(4.8) and Assumption 4.1 (ii).
Comparison of the two diagram chases up to a class from H²_G(S₀, ℤ(1)).

nodes.title: Primitive Picard correction of the trace comparison
nodes.statement: Let a ∈ Br(U)[2] satisfy the hypotheses of PI.4/uniform-obstruction-vanishing, V = U ∩ S₀ the finite-flat part, and let η, ζ be the trace-quotient lift of the Kummer lift on V (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.15/trace-quotient-lift), with b = p*η − ψ(ζ) on T_V (AT2.15/corrected-integral-lift). If β ∈ H²_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1)) lifts α_{ℝ(T)}, write β|_{T_V} = b + 2γ₀ + cl(φ₀) and p_*β = 2δ + cl(θ₁). Then there is μ ∈ Pic(S) with δ|_V − η − p_*γ₀ = cl(μ|_V).
hypotheses: n = 2; V the open where p is finite flat; the minus sign in b is essential.
proofSteps: β|_{T_V} and b both lift p*α in the topological Brauer sequence on T_V, so they differ by 2γ₀ + cl(φ₀).
p_*β induces p_*p*α = 2α = 0, so p_*β = 2δ + cl(θ₁).
Push the first identity forward: p_*b = 2η since Tr∘ψ = 0; thus 2(δ|_V − η − p_*γ₀) = cl(p_*φ₀ − θ₁|_V).
The cokernel of cl : Pic(V) → H²_G(V(ℂ), ℤ(1)) is torsion-free (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2, Benoist–Wittenberg Proposition 2.9), and Pic(S) → Pic(V) is onto, which produces μ.
acceptance: If α = 0 one may take η, ζ, β zero and μ = 0.

sources.match: Comparison of β with a lift on T_U and use of the torsion-free cokernel of Krasnov's cycle class map; the printed proof adds a mod-2 class to integral classes (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E4).
For smooth X over ℝ, the cokernel of cl : Pic(X) → H²_G(X(ℂ), ℤ(1)) is torsion-free.

nodes.title: Curve adjustment before the pushforward criterion
nodes.statement: Under Assumption 4.1 (ii), if d ∈ H²_G(S(ℂ), ℤ(1)) has [d]₁|_Ψ = 0, there is ν ∈ Pic(S), an integral combination of curves whose real loci avoid Ψ, such that [d − cl(ν)]₁ ∈ p_*H¹(T(ℝ), 𝔽₂). If moreover L(R) is ample, d − cl(ν) = p_*γ for some γ ∈ H²_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1)).
hypotheses: Assumption 4.1 (ii); for the second assertion Assumption 3.1.
proofSteps: [d]₁ lies in the kernel of H¹(S(ℝ)) → H¹(Ψ), so by (ii) it is a sum of p_*c and of cl_R(Γ_k) for curves Γ_k avoiding Ψ.
cl_R(Γ) = [cl(O(Γ))]₁ (compatibility of Krasnov and Borel–Haefliger classes; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2), so ν = Σ Γ_k works.
PI.3/equivariant-pushforward-image in degree 2 gives γ.
acceptance: If [d]₁ = 0 on all of S(ℝ), one may take ν = 0.

nodes.title: Integral pushforward adjustment for uniform evaluation
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of PI.4/uniform-obstruction-vanishing, for every β ∈ H²_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1)) lifting α_{ℝ(T)} there are γ ∈ H²_G(T(ℂ), ℤ(1)) and θ ∈ Pic(S) with p_*(β − 2γ) = cl(θ) in H²_G(S(ℂ), ℤ(1)).
hypotheses: The uniform-evaluation hypothesis; no integral lift of α̃ on U is used.
proofSteps: PI.4/primitive-picard-trace-correction gives δ|_V = η + p_*γ₀ + cl(μ|_V) with p_*β = 2δ + cl(θ₁).

Real components on Ψ ∩ V(ℝ): [p_*γ₀]₁ = p_*[γ₀]₁ vanishes on Ψ because Ψ has no real preimage (Assumption 4.1 (i)); [η]₁ on Ψ is t·cl_R(λ) by the same component computation as PI.4/uniform-first-component; so δ′ = δ − cl(μ) − t·cl(λ) has [δ′]₁ = 0 on Ψ ∩ V(ℝ), hence on Ψ by PI.1/point-removal-extension.
PI.4/curve-adjustment gives ν and γ with δ′ − cl(ν) = p_*γ.
Then p_*(β − 2γ) = 2δ + cl(θ₁) − 2(δ − cl(μ) − t cl(λ) − cl(ν)) = cl(θ) with θ = θ₁ + 2μ + 2tλ + 2ν.
acceptance: For t = 0 the λ-correction is absent.

sources.match: Existence of γ and θ with p_*(β − 2γ) = cl(θ) under the hypotheses of Proposition 4.4; the typed argument replaces the mod-2 summand (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E4–E5).

nodes.title: Proposition 4.4 for an arbitrary clopen Ψ
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1, if α has a lift α̃ ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), 𝔽₂) with [α̃]₁|_Ψ = 0, then τ = 0. Here Ψ ⊃ Θ is arbitrary, so [α̃]₀ is the indicator of Θ on Ψ and need not be constant.
hypotheses: As printed in the source; when [α̃]₀|_Ψ is constant this is PI.4/uniform-obstruction-vanishing.
proofSteps: The printed proof computes [ζ]₁|_Ψ = [e]₁|_Ψ; the computation actually gives [α̃]₀·[e]₁ (PI.4/uniform-first-component), and the Picard correction cl(φ) must then be replaced by a class whose real component on Ψ is 1_Θ·cl_R(φ), which need not be algebraic.
For constant [α̃]₀ the statement is proved by PI.4/uniform-obstruction-vanishing; the nonconstant case is the recorded gap RealSurfacePeriodIndex/G1.
acceptance: Ψ = Θ, or Ψ a union of components on which α evaluates to zero, is the uniform case.

nodes.title: Parameters for a curve on the double cover
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ, R ⊂ S an SNC divisor with equation r, A very ample and N a line bundle. For an even integer l ≫ 0 put L = A^l ⊗ N(−R); Assumption 5.1 asks H¹(S, A^l) = H¹(S, L) = H¹(S, L ⊗ N) = 0 and L, L ⊗ N very ample. For a basis (u_i) of H⁰(S, A^{l/2}), Σ u_i² has no real zeros; a general small deformation c ∈ H⁰(S, A^l) of Σ u_i² cuts out a smooth curve C = {c = 0} transverse to R in its smooth locus, with C(ℝ) = ∅ and c > 0 on S(ℝ).
hypotheses: l even and large enough for Serre vanishing and very ampleness simultaneously (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1/ample-powers-and-fixed-twists, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6).
proofSteps: Serre vanishing and very ampleness of high twists give Assumption 5.1 for all large even l.
The u_i have no common zero because A is very ample, so Σ u_i² is positive on S(ℝ) and has no real zeros.
Bertini gives a smooth transverse member among small deformations; having no real zeros and being positive on the compact S(ℝ) are open conditions.
acceptance: For S = ℙ²_ℝ, A = O(1), l = 2: Σ u_i² = x² + y² + z² defines a real-pointless conic.

sources.match: The choice L = A^l ⊗ N(−R) with the vanishing and very-ampleness conditions, and the curve C as a small deformation of a sum of squares, smooth, transverse to R and without real points.

nodes.title: The point of B whose cover contains the curve
nodes.statement: In PI.5/curve-bearing-parameters choose a general g ∈ H⁰(C, L) (reduced zeros, disjoint from R) and lift rg² ∈ H⁰(C, L²(R)) to s₀ ∈ H⁰(S, L²(R)) (possible as H¹(S, L ⊗ N) = 0). For a₁ ∈ ℝ_{>0} and a₂ ∈ H⁰(S, L ⊗ N) general, s = a₁s₀ + a₂c lies in B: its zero locus D is smooth and transverse to R in its smooth locus (Bertini off the finite base locus {c = s₀ = 0}, and a direct derivative computation there). Over C the incidence equation is rv² = a₁rg²w², and the strict transform of C splits into two copies of C, v = ±√a₁·g·w; the chosen copy C ⊂ T (v = √a₁ g w) avoids the singular points, w does not vanish on it, and w gives L|_C ≅ O_X(1)|_C. The full preimage of C also contains the ℙ¹ fibres over R ∩ C, which are not part of the lifted curve.

nodes.title: Blowing up points to realise the auxiliary hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ, R an SNC divisor and A₀ an ample line bundle with H¹(R, A₀|_R) = 0 (a sufficiently positive twist of any ample bundle works). Let μ : S′ → S be the blow-up of two disjoint finite sets P, Q of sufficiently many general closed points off R, with exceptional divisors E = μ⁻¹P, F = μ⁻¹Q, and N = μ*A₀(2F − 2E). Then there is η ∈ H¹(S′, N) with (i) H⁰(S′, N ⊗ K_{S′}) = 0, (ii) H⁰(S′, N⁻¹ ⊗ K_{S′}(R′)) = 0, (iii) H¹(R′, N|_{R′}) = 0, (iv) ∪η : H⁰(S′, K_{S′}) → H¹(S′, N ⊗ K_{S′}) injective, where R′ = μ⁻¹R ≅ R. The same holds after further blow-ups at general points off R. A₀ is unrelated to the very ample A of Proposition 6.6.
hypotheses: P, Q general and large; A₀ ample with H¹(R, A₀|_R) = 0.
proofSteps: A₀ exists: a sufficiently high power of an ample bundle has H¹(R, A₀|_R) = 0 by Serre vanishing on the curve R (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1/ample-powers-and-fixed-twists, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6).
(iii): N|_{R′} ≅ A₀|_R because the blow-ups avoid R.
(i): H⁰(S′, N ⊗ K_{S′}) = H⁰(S, A₀ ⊗ K_S ⊗ I_P) vanishes for P large and general; (ii) likewise with Q.

(iv): through the injective Leray edge maps, reduce to ν ∈ H¹(S, A₀ ⊗ I_P) with ∪ν injective on H⁰(K_S); take ν = ∂ξ for ξ ∈ H⁰(P, A₀|_P) vanishing on P₂ but at no point of P₁, where P = P₁ ⊔ P₂ is split so that no nonzero section of K_S vanishes on P₁ and none of A₀ ⊗ K_S vanishes on P₂; lift ν to H¹(S, A₀ ⊗ I_P²) and map it to H¹(S′, N).
acceptance: For S = ℙ²_ℝ and R a line, H⁰(K_S) = 0, so (iv) is empty and only (i)–(iii) need blow-ups.

sources.match: After blowing up sufficiently many general points P ∪ Q off R, N = μ*A(2F − 2E) satisfies (i)–(iv), the cup-injectivity through (5.11)–(5.12).

Assumption 6.1 asks for a compact one-manifold 𝒮 and a C^∞ embedding ι : 𝒮 → Ξ meeting R(ℝ) transversally in its smooth locus with: (i) every component of Ξ meets ι(𝒮); (ii) ι_*[𝒮] = cl_R(R) in H¹(Ξ, 𝔽₂); (iii) H¹(Ξ, 𝔽₂) is generated by the classes of the components of ι(𝒮) and the Borel–Haefliger classes of curves with real locus in Ξ; (iv) for each component Σ of Ξ, with Σ₀ = Σ ∩ (ι(𝒮) ∪ R(ℝ)) and a decomposition Σ ∖ Σ₀ = Σ₊ ⊔ Σ₋ into open and closed parts, if every point of Σ₀ is in the closures of both Σ₊ and Σ₋ then Σ₊ ∪ Σ₀ is connected.

nodes.statement: For S, R, Ξ as in PI.6/branch-locus-conditions there is a blow-up μ : S′ → S at finitely many general real points such that (S′, Ξ′ = μ⁻¹(Ξ)) with R′ the strict transform of R admits an embedding satisfying Assumption 6.1. proofSteps: Choose loops generating H¹(Ξ), add loops so every component is met, and by smooth approximation and transversality get an immersion ι : 𝒮 → Ξ transverse to R(ℝ), injective except at finitely many transverse double points, with ι_*[𝒮] = cl_R(R) and Σ ∩ (ι(𝒮) ∪ R(ℝ)) connected for each component Σ (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.12/surface-loop-representatives).

(iv): each exceptional real circle meets ι′(𝒮) in two points separating it into arcs in Σ′₊ and Σ′₋, which forces the required connectedness.

nodes.statement: Let X be a compact nonsingular affine real algebraic variety of dimension d and Y ⊂ X a compact C^∞ hypersurface. nodes.title: A branch section with prescribed real locus and sign
nodes.statement: Let A be very ample, N a line bundle, ι : 𝒮 → Ξ as in Assumption 6.1, and 𝒰 a neighbourhood of ι in C^∞(𝒮, Ξ). For every large even l there are ι′ ∈ 𝒰 and t ∈ H⁰(S, A^l ⊗ N²(−R)) such that {t = 0} is smooth along its real locus Z, Z = ι′(𝒮), and rt ∈ H⁰(S, A^l ⊗ N²) is negative on S(ℝ) ∖ Ξ.
hypotheses: Bröcker is applied to the signed divisor H − R; the printed choice (simple zero along R) leaves an extra factor 2R (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E22).
proofSteps: PI.6/nash-approximation-input gives ι′ ∈ 𝒰 and H smooth along S(ℝ) with H(ℝ) = ι′(𝒮); cl_R(H − R) = 0 by Assumption 6.1 (ii).
PI.6/brocker-sign-input (b) gives h₁ with a simple pole along R, a simple zero along H and no other real zeros or poles; (a) gives h₂ invertible along S(ℝ) with the sign of h₁ on S(ℝ) ∖ Ξ.

Let D′ be the remaining polar divisor of h₁h₂ (disjoint from S(ℝ)); choose l even with A^{l/2} ⊗ N(−R − D′) very ample, a basis (u_i) of its sections viewed in A^{l/2} ⊗ N(−R) vanishing on D′, and u = Σ u_i² ∈ H⁰(A^l ⊗ N²(−2R)).
t = −h₁h₂ r u is regular, its real zero locus is H(ℝ) (the R-orders cancel: −1 from h₁, +1 from r), and rt = −h₁h₂ r² u is negative off Ξ (PI.6/squared-line-positivity).
acceptance: If Ξ = S(ℝ) the sign condition is empty.

nodes.title: The branch conditions imply the cover hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let s ∈ H⁰(S, L²(R)) have smooth zero locus D with rs negative on S(ℝ) ∖ Ξ, let p : T → S be the double cover of PI.3/incidence-double-cover ramified over R ∪ D, and suppose the inclusion ι : 𝒮 = D(ℝ) → Ξ satisfies Assumption 6.1. Then p satisfies Assumption 4.1 with Ψ = S(ℝ) ∖ Ξ.
hypotheses: Ψ = S(ℝ) ∖ Ξ, the open and closed set to avoid (the published proof says Θ; see RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E24).
proofSteps: (i): the equation rv² = sw² has real solutions over x only if rs(x) ≥ 0, so p(T(ℝ)) ⊂ Ξ.
(ii): D lifts to T, so ι lifts to T(ℝ) and the classes of components of ι(𝒮) are pushforwards; Assumption 6.1 (iii) concludes.

(iii): for each component Σ of Ξ, p(p⁻¹Σ) = Σ₊ ∪ (Σ ∩ Δ(ℝ)) is connected by Assumption 6.1 (iv), and fibres over Δ(ℝ) are connected; if p⁻¹Σ were disconnected two components would have overlapping images and would meet over a boundary point of Δ(ℝ), a contradiction. Connected preimages give injectivity of p_* on H².
acceptance: If Ξ = S(ℝ), Ψ = ∅ and (i) is empty.

sources.match: If rs < 0 off Ξ and D(ℝ) satisfies Assumption 6.1 then p satisfies Assumption 4.1: avoidance, kernel generation and connectedness of preimages of components.

nodes.title: The vanishing variation of the double-cover family
nodes.statement: For the real family π : 𝒯 → B of PI.3/incidence-double-cover, the G-equivariant local system R²π_*ℚ on B(ℂ) splits orthogonally for the cup product as p*H²(S(ℂ), ℚ) ⊕ H²_{ℚ,van}; both are sub-variations of Hodge structure, the first constant. If λ is the class of the lifted curve C ⊂ T_s (PI.5/curve-lift) and dim coker φ_λ ≤ h²(S, O_S) (PI.5/nl-codimension-bound), then the Gauss–Manin derivative ∇λ : T_{B(ℂ),s} → H²(T, O_T)_van is surjective.
hypotheses: S connected smooth projective; p of degree 2 so p_*p* = 2 and the pullback is injective rationally.
The VHS carrier and real action are HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/geometric-real-variation over ShimuraData:D3/variation.
proofSteps: p* : H²(S, ℚ) → H²(T_b, ℚ) is injective with p_*p* = 2; its image is a constant sub-local system on which the cup pairing is nondegenerate (projection formula), so its orthogonal complement is a sub-variation (HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/orthogonal-constant-splitting).
The derivative of a constant summand vanishes (H.8/constant-symbol-zero); Griffiths' formula identifies ∇λ with φ_λ (H.8/griffiths-derivative).
The codimension bound and H²(T, O_T) = H²(S, O_S) ⊕ H²(T, O_T)_van give surjectivity onto the vanishing part (H.8/vanishing-rank-criterion).
acceptance: If h²(S, O_S) = 0 the vanishing part carries all of H²(T, O_T).

nodes.title: Transport of the chosen Kummer lift along the family
nodes.statement: Before deforming the fibre T_s in Proposition 6.6, normalise the integral lift β of the pulled-back class so that (β mod 2)|_{T_{s,U}} = p_s*α̃ (subtract cl(φ̄) for φ̄ ∈ Pic(T_s) extending the difference on T_{s,U}), and reapply PI.4/uniform-pushforward-adjustment to the normalised lift. Over a small G-stable contractible real parameter neighbourhood Λ(ℝ), transport the pair (T, p⁻¹R) equivariantly so that the restriction to T_U and the pullback of the fixed class α̃ correspond on every fibre: (β_x mod 2)|_{T_{x,U}} = p_x*α̃ for x ∈ Λ(ℝ).
hypotheses: The relative-pair transport requires an invariant Whitney stratification containing the fixed exceptional curves over Sing R and the moving ℙ¹ fibres over R ∩ D, with controlled lifts (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.16/stratified-pair-transport); verifying these for the family is the recorded gap RealSurfacePeriodIndex/G3. Direct ambient cohomological transport is an admissible alternative route.
proofSteps: The difference of β mod 2 and p_s*α̃ on T_{s,U} is the class of a line bundle there (Kummer sequence on T_{s,U}); extend it to T_s and subtract.

Ordinary equivariant Ehresmann (AT2.16/equivariant-ehresmann) trivialises 𝒯(ℂ) over Λ(ℝ); to keep track of T_U, transport the pair (T, p⁻¹R) by the stratified version (AT2.16/stratified-pair-transport) after verifying its hypotheses.
The class p*α̃ is the restriction of a class on the total space over Λ(ℝ) pulled back from U(ℂ), so its transport is the fibrewise pullback; hence the normalisation persists.
acceptance: If R = ∅ the pair is (T, ∅) and ordinary Ehresmann suffices.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.6, pp. 94–95, citing Dimca 1985, Lemma 4

nodes.title: Degree-two splitting with real-point avoidance under uniform evaluation
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ, a ∈ Br(ℝ(S)) of period 2, U its unramified locus, Θ = Θ(a), and S(ℝ) = Ξ ⊔ Ψ a decomposition into open and closed subsets with Θ ⊂ Ψ ⊂ U(ℝ). Suppose a has a Kummer lift ã ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), 𝔽₂) with [ã]₁|_Ψ = 0 and [ã]₀|_Ψ constant equal to t ∈ 𝔽₂ (t = 0 allowed, so Ψ may contain components where a evaluates to 0). Then there are a connected smooth projective surface T over ℝ and a morphism p : T → S of degree 2 with p(T(ℝ)) ⊂ Ξ and a_{ℝ(T)} = 0.
hypotheses: Uniform evaluation on Ψ; the proof uses AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.16/double-cover-diagram (gap of that packet) and the relative-pair transport of PI.6/kummer-lift-transport (gap RealSurfacePeriodIndex/G3).
proofSteps: Replace S by a modification S′ → S that is an isomorphism over U and makes S′ ∖ U an SNC divisor: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7/snc-compactification applied to the quasi-projective U with closure Y = S produces Ū → S; the ramification divisor of a on Ū is a union of components of Ū ∖ U, hence SNC, and Ψ stays open and closed in Ū(ℝ) since it is compact and open in U(ℝ); then blow up general points off R to obtain N with Assumption 5.2 (PI.5/blowup-auxiliary-bundle) and an embedding ι satisfying Assumption 6.1 (PI.6/branch-conditions-blowup); modifications off U do not change the hypotheses.
Choose A very ample, L = A^l ⊗ N(−R) with l large even so that Assumptions 3.1, 5.1 and PI.6/signed-branch-section hold; get t with rt negative on Ψ and real locus ι(𝒮).

Take s = a₁s₀ + a₂c (PI.5/curve-lift) with a₁ > 0 small and a₂ near t; then rs < 0 on Ψ, D(ℝ) = ι(𝒮) after moving ι (PI.6/branch-conditions-stable), and p satisfies Assumption 4.1 (PI.6/topology-to-cover-hypotheses).

PI.4/pullback-unramified, PI.4/uniform-obstruction-vanishing and PI.4/uniform-pushforward-adjustment give a_T ∈ Br(T)[2], an integral lift β normalised as in PI.6/kummer-lift-transport, and γ, θ with p_*(β − 2γ) = cl(θ).

Split β − 2γ = (ε₁, ε₂) along p*H²(S) ⊕ H²_van (PI.6/vanishing-variation); the invariant equivariant classes map to a full lattice of H²(T, ℝ(1))^G_van (AT2.16/finite-index-lattice); the real Green cone (HodgeStructuresPartII:H.8/vanishing-real-green) meets ε₂ + 2·lattice (H.8/full-lattice-coset-cone): ε₂ = 2δ + ν with ν in the cone.

For some x ∈ Λ(ℝ), ν is of type (1,1) on T_x and ε₁ is of type (1,1) because p_*(β − 2γ) = cl(θ); so β − 2γ − 2δ is an integral equivariant (1,1) class and the real Lefschetz (1,1) theorem (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.7) writes it as cl(φ) on T_x.
By the transported normalisation, a vanishes on T_{x,U} in the Kummer sequence, hence in Br(ℝ(T_x)); replace T by T_x. p(T_x(ℝ)) ⊂ Ξ for x near s.
acceptance: If S(ℝ) = ∅ (Theorem 0.3 setting), Ψ = Ξ = ∅ and the conclusion is a degree-2 splitting cover of S.
For t = 0 the theorem applies to a = (n/2)α with 4 | n and Ψ = Θ(α).

sources.match: Existence of a degree-2 cover T → S with p(T(ℝ)) ⊂ Ξ splitting α, by the double-cover family, Propositions 4.2–4.5, Green's real criterion and the real Lefschetz (1,1) theorem.
Real Lefschetz (1,1): integral equivariant classes of type (1,1) are classes of real line bundles.

hypotheses: As printed; its proof uses PI.4/obstruction-vanishing-general and PI.4/pushforward-adjustment-general, which carry gap RealSurfacePeriodIndex/G1.
proofSteps: The proof of PI.6/degree-two-splitting-uniform goes through verbatim once the general Propositions 4.4–4.5 are available; they are not, outside the uniform case.

nodes.title: Uniform evaluation of the half-period class
nodes.statement: Let α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)) have even period n, U = U_α, and Ψ = Θ(α), assumed to be a union of components of S(ℝ) contained in U(ℝ). The period-2 class a = (n/2)α evaluates at every x ∈ Ψ to (n/2 mod 2)·(−1,−1) and to 0 at every x ∈ U(ℝ) ∖ Ψ. Hence any Kummer lift of a restricted to U(ℂ) has [·]₀|_Ψ constant equal to t = n/2 mod 2: t = 1 if n ≡ 2 mod 4 and t = 0 if 4 | n; in the latter case Θ(a) = ∅ although Ψ need not be empty.
hypotheses: n even; Θ(α) a union of components of S(ℝ) inside U(ℝ).
proofSteps: α_x ∈ Br(ℝ) ≅ ℤ/2 equals the nonzero element on Ψ and 0 off Ψ; multiplying by n/2 gives the stated values.
The degree-zero component of a Kummer lift is the evaluation (PI.1/real-evaluation-locus).
acceptance: For n = 2, t = 1 and Θ(a) = Θ(α).
For n = 4, t = 0.

sources.match: Proposition 6.6 is applied to (n/2)α with Ψ = Θ and Ξ = S(ℝ) ∖ Θ.

nodes.title: The induction step on the period
nodes.statement: Let α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)) have even period n, with Θ(α) a union of components of S(ℝ) and a lift ξ ∈ H²_G(U_α(ℂ), 𝔽₂) of (n/2)α with [ξ]₁|_{Θ(α)} = 0. Then there is a degree-2 morphism p : T → S of connected smooth projective real surfaces with p(T(ℝ)) ∩ Θ(α) = ∅ such that α_{ℝ(T)} has period exactly n/2 and evaluates to 0 at every real point of its unramified locus.
hypotheses: The setting of PI.7/half-period-uniform-evaluation.
proofSteps: a = (n/2)α has unramified locus U_a ⊃ U_α; lift a on U_a and compare with ξ on U_α: the difference is the reduction of a Picard class of U_α, which extends to U_a (PI.1/point-removal-extension); subtract it to get a lift ã on U_a restricting to ξ.
Ψ = Θ(α) is a union of components inside U_α(ℝ) ⊂ U_a(ℝ), Θ(a) ⊂ Ψ by density of U_α and local constancy, and [ã]₀|_Ψ is constant (PI.7/half-period-uniform-evaluation).
PI.6/degree-two-splitting-uniform with Ξ = S(ℝ) ∖ Ψ gives p : T → S of degree 2 with a_{ℝ(T)} = 0 and p(T(ℝ)) ∩ Ψ = ∅.
Period: m = per(α_{ℝ(T)}) divides n/2 since (n/2)α_T = a_T = 0; corestriction (SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII:SA.1/corestriction-restriction-degree) gives cor(α_T) = 2α, of period n/2, so n/2 divides m.

Evaluation: for y ∈ V(ℝ), V the unramified locus of α_T, either y ∈ p⁻¹(U)(ℝ), where α_T(y) = α(p(y)) = 0 as p(y) ∉ Θ, or y lies in a component of V(ℝ) meeting p⁻¹(U)(ℝ) densely; local constancy gives α_T(y) = 0.

sources.match: Apply Proposition 6.6 to (n/2)α with Ψ = Θ; α_{ℝ(T)} has period n/2 and vanishes at real points, and induction concludes.
The odd case is handled by de Jong and a norm argument; the half-period lift condition concerns even n (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E8).

nodes.title: Sufficient condition for period equals index
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ and α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)) of period n, U = U_α, Θ = Θ(α), assumed to be a union of components of S(ℝ). If n is odd, ind(α) = n. If n is even and some lift ξ ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), 𝔽₂) of (n/2)α has [ξ]₁|_Θ = 0, then ind(α) = n.
hypotheses: The odd case needs no lift condition.
proofSteps: Odd n: PI.1/real-closed-norm-bound.

Even n, by induction on n: PI.7/period-induction-step gives p : T → S of degree 2 with α_T of period n/2 evaluating to 0 at all real points of its unramified locus; then Θ(α_T) = ∅ and the lift condition holds trivially for α_T (zero first component on the empty set), so by induction (or by the odd case) ind(α_T) = n/2.
Reverse index divisibility: ind(α) divides 2·ind(α_T) = n (SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII:SA.0/index-divides-degree-index), and n = per(α) divides ind(α).
acceptance: For α of period 2 with Θ = ∅ and any lift, ind(α) = 2.

sources.match: If Θ is a union of components and the half-period lift has vanishing first component on Θ, then ind(α) = n, by induction on n.

planet.name: Sufficient condition for period equals index

nodes.title: Period equals index on real surfaces without real points
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ with S(ℝ) = ∅. Then ind(α) = per(α) for every α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)), ramified or not.
hypotheses: S connected smooth projective over ℝ, S(ℝ) = ∅.
proofSteps: Θ = ∅ is a union of components of the empty S(ℝ), and the lift condition is empty; apply PI.7/arbitrary-period-sufficiency.
acceptance: For S the anisotropic quadric x² + y² + z² + w² = 0 in ℙ³_ℝ, every class of Br(ℝ(S)) has index equal to its period.
K = ℝ(x, y, z | x² + y² + z² = −1) is a field of cohomological dimension 2 on which period equals index.

sources.match: If S(ℝ) = ∅ then ind(α) = per(α) for every α ∈ Br(ℝ(S)); it is the case S(ℝ) = ∅ of Proposition 6.7.

nodes.title: Period equals index for classes vanishing at real points
nodes.statement: Let U be a connected smooth surface over ℝ and α ∈ Br(U) ⊂ Br(ℝ(U)) with α_x = 0 ∈ Br(ℝ) for every x ∈ U(ℝ). Then ind(α) = per(α).
hypotheses: U connected smooth over ℝ, not necessarily proper; U is quasi-projective (a smooth separated surface over a field is, by Nagata compactification, resolution of surface singularities and Zariski's projectivity of smooth proper surfaces).
proofSteps: Compactify U to a connected smooth projective S with ℝ(S) = ℝ(U) (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7/snc-compactification); then U ⊂ U_α.

Each component of S(ℝ) is a smooth surface and S ∖ U meets it in a set of dimension ≤ 1, so U(ℝ) is dense in S(ℝ) and in U_α(ℝ); evaluation is locally constant on U_α(ℝ) (PI.1/real-evaluation-locus) and vanishes on U(ℝ), hence Θ(α) = ∅.
Apply PI.7/arbitrary-period-sufficiency with Θ = ∅, a union of (no) components, for which the lift condition is empty.
acceptance: For α = (−1, 1 + x²) on 𝔸², α_x = 0 everywhere and ind α = per α = 1 (α = 0).

sources.match: If α ∈ Br(U) vanishes at every real point of U then ind(α) = per(α); it is Proposition 6.7 with Θ = ∅.

nodes.title: Unramified classes: the sufficient half of Theorem 0.5
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ and α ∈ Br(S) of period n. If n is odd, or if some lift ξ ∈ H²_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) of (n/2)α in the Kummer sequence 0 → Pic(S)/2 → H²_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) → Br(S)[2] → 0 satisfies [ξ]₁|_Θ = 0, then ind(α) = per(α).
hypotheses: α unramified on S, so U = S and Θ = Θ(α) is a union of components of S(ℝ).
proofSteps: Apply PI.7/arbitrary-period-sufficiency with U = S.
acceptance: If S(ℝ) is orientable and every class of H¹(S(ℝ)) is algebraic, the condition can be met by a Picard correction.

sources.match: Odd period, or existence of a half-period lift with vanishing first component on Θ, implies ind = per; it is Proposition 6.7 with U = S.

nodes.title: Vanishing at real closures implies vanishing at real points
nodes.statement: Let U be a smooth real surface and α ∈ Br(U)[2]. If α vanishes at every real closure of ℝ(U), then α_x = 0 for every x ∈ U(ℝ).
hypotheses: α unramified on U.
proofSteps: At x ∈ U(ℝ) choose local parameters z₁, z₂; the completion embeds ℝ(U) into ℝ((z₁, z₂)), which embeds into a real closed field K such as the iterated Puiseux field ⋃_{n₂}(⋃_{n₁} ℝ((z₁^{1/n₁})))((z₂^{1/n₂})).

In Br(ℝ) → Br(ℝ[[z₁, z₂]]) → Br(K), the first map is an isomorphism with retraction given by restriction to x (henselian local rings, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.22 brauer_henselian_local), and the composite is an isomorphism because both groups are generated by (−1, −1) (PI.0/real-closure-at-ordering).
α_K = 0 (K is a real closure of ℝ(U) at the induced ordering), so α_x = 0.
acceptance: For α = (−1, −1) pulled back to U, α does not vanish at real closures when U(ℝ) ≠ ∅, consistently.

sources.match: For x ∈ U(ℝ), local parameters and a real closed extension of ℝ((z₁, z₂)) show that α vanishes at x, via Br(ℝ) → Br(ℝ[[z₁, z₂]]) → Br(K).

nodes.title: The Elman–Lam invariant in transcendence degree two
nodes.statement: Let K be a field extension of ℝ of transcendence degree 2, not necessarily finitely generated. Then u(K) ≤ 4 (Elman–Lam invariant).
hypotheses: trdeg_ℝ K = 2.
proofSteps: By PI.0/pfister-brauer-criterion it suffices that every nonzero α ∈ Br(K)[2] vanishing at all real closures of K has index 2.

Choose a finitely generated K₀ ⊂ K containing a transcendence basis of K/ℝ and over which α is defined (so K/K₀ is algebraic; RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E9), write K as the union of the finite extensions K_i of K₀, and α_i ∈ Br(K_i)[2]. The sets Z_i ⊂ X_{K_i} of orderings where α_i survives are closed (PI.0/brauer-nonvanishing-locus) with empty limit, so some Z_i is empty (PI.0/harrison-compact): replace K by K_i.

Now K = ℝ(S) for an integral surface; let U be an open with α ∈ Br(U); α_x = 0 for x ∈ U(ℝ) (PI.7/real-closure-pointwise-triviality), so ind(α) = 2 by PI.7/zero-evaluation-period-index (on the smooth locus).
acceptance: u(ℝ(x, y)) ≤ 4, new before Benoist.

sources.locator: Theorem 0.12, first assertion, p. 66; proof, pp. 95–96
sources.match: u(K) ≤ 4 for every extension of ℝ of transcendence degree 2, by Pfister's criterion, compactness of orderings and Theorem 0.4.

nodes.title: A four-dimensional anisotropic zero-signature form
nodes.statement: Let S be an integral surface over ℝ and x a smooth closed point with κ(x) ≅ ℂ. Let w ∈ O_{S,x} lift √−1 and replace it by w′ = (w² − 1)/(2w), which again lifts √−1 and satisfies w′² + 1 = (w² + 1)²/(4w²) ∈ m_x². For any regular system of parameters z₁, z₂ at x, y_j = (1 + z_j)² + (w′ + z_j)² (j = 1, 2) is again a regular system of parameters, each y_j is a sum of two squares (hence positive at every ordering), and q = ⟨1, y₁, −y₂, −y₁y₂⟩ has zero total signature and is anisotropic over ℝ(S).
hypotheses: x smooth with residue field ℂ (exists on any integral surface over ℝ); the replacement of w is the corrected choice (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E10).
proofSteps: dy_j = 2(1 + z_j)dz_j + 2(w′ + z_j)(dw′ + dz_j) ≡ 2(1 + i)dz_j modulo m_x and the differential of w′² + 1 ∈ m_x², so y₁, y₂ are regular parameters.
Completion gives ℝ(S) ⊂ ℂ((y₁))((y₂)) (κ(x) = ℂ); by PI.0/springer-complete-dvr applied twice, q is anisotropic there, hence over ℝ(S) (anisotropy descends to subfields).
y_j is a sum of two squares, so y_j >_P 0 at every ordering and sign_P(q) = 1 + 1 − 1 − 1 = 0.
acceptance: For S = 𝔸² and x the closed point corresponding to (i, 0), the construction gives an explicit anisotropic form over ℝ(x, y).

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 0.12, lower bound, p. 96
sources.match: At a closed point with residue field ℂ, the y_j built from a lift of √−1 are local parameters and ⟨1, y₁, −y₂, −y₁y₂⟩ is anisotropic over ℂ((y₁))((y₂)) by Springer, with y_j totally positive.

nodes.title: Quadratic forms of rank five over surfaces without real points
nodes.statement: Let S be an integral surface over ℝ with S(ℝ) = ∅. Every quadratic form of rank ≥ 5 over ℝ(S) is isotropic.
hypotheses: S(ℝ) = ∅, so ℝ(S) is nonreal (no orderings) on a smooth projective model, and the Elman–Lam invariant is the classical one.
proofSteps: ℝ(S) is nonreal: by the Artin–Lang theorem the function field of an integral real variety is real iff the variety has a smooth real point, and S has no real points at all.

nodes.title: Degree-four del Pezzo surfaces over real curves without real points
nodes.statement: Let C be an integral curve over ℝ with C(ℝ) = ∅. Every del Pezzo surface of degree 4 over ℝ(C) has an ℝ(C)-rational point.
hypotheses: A degree-4 del Pezzo surface over a field F is, through its anticanonical embedding, a smooth complete intersection of two quadrics in ℙ⁴_F (cited classical input).
proofSteps: Write the surface as {q₁ = q₂ = 0} ⊂ ℙ⁴ over F = ℝ(C).
F(t) = ℝ(C × ℙ¹) is the function field of an integral surface without real points, so q₁ + tq₂ (rank 5) is isotropic over F(t) by PI.7/rank-five-isotropy.
Amer–Brumer (PI.0/amer-brumer) gives a common nonzero zero of q₁, q₂ over F, a rational point.
acceptance: When C is the anisotropic conic, this is equivalent to the real integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles on degree-4 del Pezzo fibrations over C (Benoist–Wittenberg II, Proposition 8.3).

nodes.title: The finite-flat open and the restricted evaluation locus
nodes.statement: Let p : T → S be a generically finite morphism of connected smooth projective real surfaces of even degree n, α ∈ Br(ℝ(S))[n] with p*α = 0, U = U_α and Θ = Θ(α). Let U₀ ⊂ U be the largest open over which p is finite flat with smooth branch locus Δ ∩ U₀; U ∖ U₀ is finite. Put Θ₀ = Θ ∩ U₀(ℝ). Then p(T(ℝ)) ∩ Θ = ∅, and Θ₀ is contained in the étale locus V of the alternating double cover (PI.8/alternating-double-cover).
hypotheses: n even; p*α = 0 in Br(ℝ(T)).
proofSteps: If y ∈ T(ℝ) with p(y) ∈ Θ, then α_{p(y)} = (p*α)_y = 0 after restricting to a real point, contradicting p(y) ∈ Θ (evaluation commutes with pullback; p*α is unramified near y).
A finite-type map of smooth surfaces is flat where it is finite (miracle flatness), and the locus where the branch divisor is not smooth or p not finite is finite in U.
If x ∈ Δ_i(ℝ) ∩ Θ₀ with m_i odd, a general such x has geometric fibre of odd cardinality n − m_i, so a real preimage, contradicting the first point; hence Θ₀ ⊂ V(ℝ).
acceptance: If p is finite étale over U then U₀ = U and Θ₀ = Θ.

nodes.title: The alternating double cover and branch multiplicities
nodes.statement: For p : T → S as in PI.8/finite-flat-open with étale locus S* (degree n), compose the monodromy π₁^ét(S*) → 𝔖_n with the sign to get a finite étale double cover Ŝ* → S*, independent of the numbering; its normalisation Ŝ → S is a finite double cover. For a branch component Δ_i with geometric generic fibre F_i put m_i = n − |F_i| = Σ_{y ∈ F_i}(e_y − 1). The maximal open over which Ŝ → S is étale is V = S ∖ ⋃_{m_i odd} Δ_i.
hypotheses: Purity of the branch locus (Zariski–Nagata) for the normal double cover.
proofSteps: The sign of the monodromy is a homomorphism to ℤ/2, giving the double cover; renumbering conjugates the monodromy and does not change the sign. Étale and topological double covers of S* correspond through the finite-coefficient comparison (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.3/finite-coefficient-comparison in degree 1).
Local monodromy around Δ_i is a permutation with cycle type given by the ramification indices; it is odd iff m_i is odd.
The branch locus of the normal double cover has pure codimension one, so V is as stated.
acceptance: For n = 2, m_i = 1 for every branch component, and V = S ∖ Δ.

nodes.title: Lifting the Kummer class through the trace sequence
nodes.statement: In PI.8/finite-flat-open let α̃ ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), ℤ/n(1)) lift α in the Kummer sequence. Then α̃|_{U₀} = η mod n − φ(ζ) for some η ∈ H²_G(U₀(ℂ), ℤ(1)) and ζ ∈ H²_G(U₀(ℂ), Q(1)), where Q = coker(ℤ → p_*ℤ) and φ : Q → ℤ/n is induced by the trace.
hypotheses: p finite over U₀, so the Leray spectral sequence of T_{U₀} → U₀ degenerates.
proofSteps: The obstruction is the image of α̃|_{U₀} in H³_G(U₀(ℂ), p_*ℤ(1)) ≅ H³_G(T_{U₀}(ℂ), ℤ(1)).
Comparing the Kummer sequence with the trace sequence 0 → p_*ℤ → ℤ ⊕ Q → ℤ/n → 0, this image is the topological obstruction of p*α|_{U₀}, which vanishes since p*α = 0.
Apply AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.15/trace-quotient-lift.
acceptance: If α = 0 one can take η = ζ = 0.

sources.match: α̃|_{U₀} is the image under (1, −φ) of (η, ζ), because its boundary vanishes in H³_G(T_{U₀}(ℂ), ℤ(1)).

nodes.title: The sign-corrected pullback lift
nodes.statement: With η, ζ from PI.8/trace-quotient-lift-surface and ψ : Q → p_*ℤ the trace-zero operator, p*α̃|_{U₀} ∈ H²_G(T_{U₀}(ℂ), ℤ/n(1)) is the reduction modulo n of p*η − ψ(ζ). (The published Lemma 7.3 and (7.13) have +ψ(ζ).)
hypotheses: The minus sign matches the convention (1, −φ); equality of maps Q → p_*(ℤ/n) is checked on the target, which injects into j_*j*.
proofSteps: α̃ = η mod n − φ(ζ); p*(η mod n) = (p*η) mod n.
ψ mod n = p*∘φ as maps Q → p_*(ℤ/n): they agree on étale stalks and p_*(ℤ/n) → j_*j*p_*(ℤ/n) is injective (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.15/trace-zero-operator); hence p*φ(ζ) = ψ(ζ) mod n.
This is AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.15/corrected-integral-lift on the surface.
acceptance: Tr(p*η − ψ(ζ)) = nη, since Tr∘ψ = 0.

sources.match: p*α̃ is the reduction of p*η + ψ(ζ), via diagrams (7.3)–(7.4); the sign must be minus (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E6) and the injectivity used concerns the target sheaf (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E7).

nodes.title: The circle double cover attached to the quotient class
nodes.statement: Let ι : 𝕊¹ → Θ₀ be a C^∞ embedding meeting the branch locus of p transversally at general points. On 𝕊¹ the permutation stalks of p_*ℤ are free ℤ[G]-modules (no real sheets). The sheaf 𝒢 = coker[(φ₂, 1 + σ) : ι*Q(1) → 𝔽₂ ⊕ (ι*Q(1))^G] sits in an exact sequence 0 → 𝔽₂ → 𝒢 → 𝔽₂ → 0 (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.15/circle-extension), with stalks 𝔽₂² if 4 | n and ℤ/4 if n ≡ 2 mod 4. The elements of 𝒢 mapping to 1 form a double cover ρ̃ : 𝕊̃¹ → 𝕊¹ whose class ε̃ ∈ H¹(𝕊¹, 𝔽₂) is the boundary of 1, namely ι*[φ(ζ)]₁.
hypotheses: n even; ι transverse to the branch locus (such embedded circles represent every class of H₁(Θ₀, 𝔽₂): AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.12/surface-loop-representatives); the input ζ has normalised degree-two component 1 because φ(ζ)|_x = −α̃|_x ≠ 0 at x ∈ 𝕊¹ ⊂ Θ.
proofSteps: Ext stalks: (Ext^q_G(ℤ, ι*p_*ℤ))_x = H^q(G, ℤ[G]^k) = 0 for q > 0 (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.14/equivariant-ext-stalk).

AT2.15/circle-extension gives exactness and identifies the boundary of 1 with the degree-one component of φζ; the degree-zero normalisation holds because η|_x = 0 (H²(G, ℤ(1)) = 0) and α̃|_x ≠ 0 on Θ.
The reduction from ℤ/n(1) to 𝔽₂ on the two twisted cyclic degrees is (id, n/2 mod 2) (AT2.15/cyclic-reduction-degrees), which gives the stalk computation and forbids treating both cases as split.
acceptance: For n = 2 the stalks are ℤ/4.

sources.match: The sheaf 𝒢 on 𝕊¹, the exact sequence (7.6), and the identification of the boundary of 1 with ι*[φ(ζ)]₁; stalks 𝔽₂ ⊕ 𝔽₂ if 4 | n and ℤ/4 otherwise.

nodes.title: Local monodromy correction of circle covers
nodes.statement: In PI.8/circle-double-cover let ε̂ ∈ H¹(𝕊¹, 𝔽₂) be the class of the pullback of the alternating double cover ((ι*ê)). Then ε̃ = ε̂ + Σ_{4 ∤ m_i} ι*cl_R(Δ_i) in H¹(𝕊¹, 𝔽₂). On Θ₀ every m_i met by 𝕊¹ is even, and the local discrepancy at a crossing with Δ_i is m_i/2 mod 2.
hypotheses: ι meets the branch components at general points of Δ_i(ℝ) ∩ Θ₀.
proofSteps: Off the finitely many crossings, a canonical bijection χ_x between the fibres of the two covers comes from orderings (a₁, …, a_{n/2}, σa₁, …, σa_{n/2}) of p⁻¹(x) up to even permutations and the functions equal to √−1 on the a_j and 0 on the σa_j.
At a crossing with Δ_i, the monodromy of a small loop exchanges the a's with conjugates of the b's in a way whose two permutations have the same cycle type, odd iff 4 ∤ m_i; so χ extends iff 4 | m_i.
Each nonextending crossing contributes ι*cl_R(Δ_i).
acceptance: If no branch component meets 𝕊¹, ε̃ = ε̂.
