nodes.title: Obstruction to splitting by an even-degree cover
nodes.statement: Let p : T → S be a generically finite morphism of even degree n between connected smooth projective real surfaces, α ∈ Br(ℝ(S))[n] with p*α = 0, U = U_α, Θ = Θ(α), α̃ ∈ H²_G(U(ℂ), ℤ/n(1)) a Kummer lift and ξ its reduction modulo 2. Then [ξ]₁|_Θ = cl_R(ν)|_Θ for some ν ∈ Pic(S).
hypotheses: n even.
proofSteps: PI.8/corrected-pullback-lift: p*α̃|_{U₀} = (p*η − ψ(ζ)) mod n; p*α|_{U₀} = 0 gives p*η − ψ(ζ) = nγ + cl(ϕ) on T_{U₀} (real topological Brauer sequence, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2).
Push forward: p_*ψ(ζ) = 0, so n(η − p_*γ) = cl(p_*ϕ); torsion-freeness of the cokernel of cl on Pic(U₀) and extension to S give μ with η − p_*γ = cl(μ|_{U₀}), hence [η]₁ − p_*[γ]₁ = cl_R(μ) on U₀(ℝ).
p_*[γ]₁ vanishes on Θ₀ (no real preimages); with PI.8/quotient-component-algebraicity, [ξ]₁ = [η]₁ + [φ(ζ)]₁ = cl_R(μ + θ) on Θ₀.
H¹(Θ) → H¹(Θ₀) is injective (PI.1/point-removal-extension), so the identity holds on Θ.
acceptance: If T(ℝ) = ∅ and Θ = S(ℝ), the conclusion says [ξ]₁ is algebraic on all of S(ℝ).

sources.match: If p*α = 0 for an even-degree p then [ξ]₁|_Θ = cl_R(ν)|_Θ, by Lemma 7.3, pushforward, primitivity of the Picard image and Proposition 7.4.

nodes.title: Unramified classes: the obstruction half of Theorem 0.5
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ and α ∈ Br(S) of even period n. If no lift ξ ∈ H²_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) of (n/2)α satisfies [ξ]₁|_Θ = 0, then ind(α) = 2n.
hypotheses: α unramified on S; the criterion is existential in the lift.
proofSteps: ind(α) ∈ {n, 2n} (PI.1/real-closed-norm-bound). Suppose ind(α) = n: take a degree-n splitting field L of ℝ(S) (SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII:SA.0/class-index-attained), the normalisation N of S in L (finite over S), and a resolution T → N with T smooth projective and connected (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7/snc-compactification with closure Y = N); p : T → S is generically finite of degree n.
Let α̃ ∈ H²_G(S(ℂ), ℤ/n(1)) lift α; its reduction ξ lifts (n/2)α, and PI.8/even-degree-splitting-obstruction gives ν with [ξ]₁|_Θ = cl_R(ν)|_Θ.
ξ′ = ξ − (cl(ν) mod 2) is another lift of (n/2)α with [ξ′]₁|_Θ = 0 (compatibility of cl and cl_R), contradicting the hypothesis.

nodes.title: Image of the first two real components
nodes.statement: Let S be a connected smooth projective surface over ℝ with total Stiefel–Whitney class w = (w_i) of S(ℝ). The image of ρ : H²_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) → H⁰(S(ℝ)) ⊕ H¹(S(ℝ)), restriction followed by the canonical decomposition and projection, is the set of (a₀, a₁) with deg([δ]₁ ∪ (a₁ + a₀ ∪ w₁)) = 0 for every δ ∈ H¹_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) with [δ]₀ = 0.
hypotheses: 𝔽₂ coefficients; deg the mod-2 degree on H²(S(ℝ)).
proofSteps: The localisation sequence with supports on S(ℝ) is canonically split (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.9/mod-two-splitting), giving H²_G = H²_{G,S(ℝ)} ⊕ H²_G(S(ℂ) ∖ S(ℝ)).

Equivariant purity identifies H²_{G,S(ℝ)} with H⁰(S(ℝ)), and its image under ρ is {(a₀, a₀ ∪ w₁)}, since the self-intersection class γ is the total Stiefel–Whitney class (AT2.9/gamma-class, AT2.12/gamma-stiefel-whitney).
The image of the complement factor is {(0, a₁)} with a₁ orthogonal to all [δ]₁ with [δ]₀ = 0, by the self-duality of the corrected localisation sequence (AT2.10/localization-self-dual).
acceptance: If S(ℝ) = ∅ the image is 0.

nodes.title: Real Enriques surfaces and their two halves
nodes.statement: A real Enriques surface is a smooth projective geometrically connected surface S over ℝ with S_ℂ an Enriques surface (EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence:E0/is-enriques; in characteristic 0: q = p_g = 0 and K_S of order 2). The two lifts of K_S ∈ Pic(S)[2] in H¹_ét(S, μ₂) ≅ H¹_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) define the two real forms Y₁, Y₂ → S of the canonical K3 double cover; their real images are the halves S₁, S₂ of S, open and closed with S(ℝ) = S₁ ⊔ S₂, either of which may be empty.
hypotheses: The canonical cover is the étale K3 cover (EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence:E3/etale-canonical-is-k3 in characteristic ≠ 2).
The two lifts differ by the constant class of ℝˣ/ℝˣ² in the degree-one Kummer sequence 0 → ℝˣ/ℝˣ² → H¹_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) → Pic(S)[2] → 0.
proofSteps: Pic(S) → Pic(S_ℂ) is injective (Hilbert 90 for H¹(G, ℂˣ)), Pic(S_ℂ)[2] = {0, K} by the Enriques invariants (EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence:E0/pic-tau-length), and K_S is defined over ℝ, so Pic(S)[2] = {0, K_S}.
Each lift is a finite étale double cover, a real form of the canonical cover; a real point x of S lifts to exactly one of the two forms, which defines the partition of S(ℝ).
acceptance: If S(ℝ) = ∅ both halves are empty.
Each half is a union of components of S(ℝ).

nodes.title: The Brauer group of a real Enriques surface is killed by four
nodes.statement: For a real Enriques surface S, H²(S, O_S) = 0 and H³(S(ℂ), ℤ)_tors ≅ ℤ/2, so Br(S_ℂ) ≅ ℤ/2 by the complex topological Brauer sequence; restriction and corestriction to S_ℂ show that Br(S) is killed by 4.
hypotheses: Enriques invariants from EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence:E0/geometric-invariants; π₁ of S(ℂ) is ℤ/2.
proofSteps: In characteristic 0, q = p_g = 0 (requested from EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence:E0; E0/geometric-invariants gives h¹(O) = h²(O) ≤ 1), so every class of H²(S(ℂ), ℤ) is algebraic by integral Lefschetz (1,1) and Br(S_ℂ) ≅ H³(S(ℂ), ℤ)_tors, which is ℤ/2 (Poincaré duality H³ ≅ H₁ and π₁ = ℤ/2).
cor ∘ res = 2 on Br(S), and res lands in a group killed by 2.
acceptance: Br(S_ℂ) has exactly two elements.

sources.match: Br(S_ℂ) ≅ H³(S(ℂ), ℤ)_tors = ℤ/2 by (1.2), so Br(S) is 4-torsion; Mangolte–van Hamel compute it precisely.

nodes.title: Detecting an empty half
nodes.statement: Let S be a real Enriques surface with S(ℝ) ≠ ∅. In 0 → ℝˣ/ℝˣ² → H¹_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) → Pic(S)[2] → 0 the constant nonzero class has degree-zero component 1. A nonzero δ ∈ H¹_G(S(ℂ), 𝔽₂) with [δ]₀ = 0 exists iff exactly one half of S is empty; it is then unique, and [δ]₁ = cl_R(K_S) = w₁(S(ℝ)).
hypotheses: S(ℝ) ≠ ∅ (if S(ℝ) = ∅ all three nonzero classes have zero restriction and uniqueness fails).
proofSteps: H¹_G has four elements: 0, the constant class c (with [c]₀ = 1 on S(ℝ)), and the two lifts of K_S; [·]₀ of a lift of K_S is the indicator of the complement of its half.
A lift with [δ]₀ = 0 exists iff its half is all of S(ℝ), that is iff the other half is empty; it is unique since the two lifts differ by c.
[δ]₁ = cl_R(υ(δ)) = cl_R(K_S) (Lemma 2.1 of the source, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2) and cl_R(K_S) = w₁ (Kahn 1987, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.2).
acceptance: If both halves are nonempty, no such δ exists.

sources.match: The degree-one Kummer sequence, the two preimages of K_S, and [δ]₁ = cl_R(K_S) = w₁ by Lemma 2.1 and Kahn's theorem; uniqueness of the nonzero δ (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E15).

nodes.title: Orientable or empty real locus
nodes.statement: If S is a real Enriques surface with S(ℝ) empty or orientable, every α ∈ Br(S) has ind(α) = per(α).
hypotheses: S real Enriques.
proofSteps: S(ℝ) = ∅: PI.7/no-real-points-period-index.
Br(S) is killed by 4 (PI.9/enriques-complex-brauer); classes of period 4 have index 4 (PI.9/enriques-period-four).

For α of period 2 and any lift α̃, cl_R is onto when S(ℝ) is orientable (PI.9/enriques-picard-image), so [α̃]₁ = cl_R(θ) = [cl(θ)]₁ and α̃ − (cl(θ) mod 2) is a lift with zero first component; PI.7/unramified-odd-or-vanishing gives index 2.
acceptance: Real Enriques surfaces whose real locus is a union of spheres and tori satisfy period = index for all unramified classes.

sources.match: If S(ℝ) is empty or orientable, every period-2 class has a lift with [α̃]₁ = 0, so index 2.

nodes.title: Two nonempty halves and a nonorientable real locus
nodes.statement: If S(ℝ) is nonorientable and both halves of S are nonempty, there is α ∈ Br(S) of period 2 and index 4.
hypotheses: S real Enriques; both halves nonempty; w₁ ≠ 0.
proofSteps: No nonzero δ with [δ]₀ = 0 exists (PI.9/enriques-half-detector), so by PI.9/real-locus-image every (1, a₁) is in the image of ρ; choose a₁ ∉ im cl_R (cl_R is not onto since w₁ ≠ 0).
The induced α has Θ = S(ℝ) and no lift with zero first component: lifts differ by Picard classes, whose components are cl_R; PI.8/unramified-index-doubling gives index 4.
acceptance: Such surfaces exist (Degtyarev–Itenberg–Kharlamov classification).

sources.match: When both halves are nonempty, Proposition 8.1 gives a lift with [α̃]₀ = 1 and [α̃]₁ outside im cl_R; its class has index 4.

nodes.title: One nonempty half with an odd number of odd-Euler components
nodes.statement: If S(ℝ) is nonorientable, exactly one half is nonempty and deg(w₁²) ≠ 0 (equivalently S(ℝ) has an odd number of components of odd Euler characteristic), then there is α ∈ Br(S) of period 2 and index 4.
hypotheses: deg(w₁(Σ)²) ≡ χ(Σ) mod 2 for each component Σ (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.12/gamma-stiefel-whitney).
proofSteps: With δ the unique class of PI.9/enriques-half-detector, [δ]₁ = w₁, and PI.9/real-locus-image gives a lift with components (1, w₁) since deg(w₁ ∪ (w₁ + w₁)) = 0.
w₁ ∉ im cl_R because deg(w₁ ∪ w₁) ≠ 0 (PI.9/enriques-picard-image); conclude by PI.8/unramified-index-doubling.
acceptance: A real Enriques surface with real locus a single ℝℙ² in one half is an example.

nodes.title: One nonempty half with an even number of odd-Euler components
nodes.statement: If exactly one half of S is nonempty and deg(w₁²) = 0, every period-2 class α ∈ Br(S) has index 2.
hypotheses: S real Enriques; S(ℝ) ≠ ∅.
proofSteps: For a lift α̃, PI.9/real-locus-image gives deg([α̃]₁ ∪ w₁ + [α̃]₀ ∪ w₁²) = 0.
If deg([α̃]₁ ∪ w₁) = 0 take a = [α̃]₁; otherwise some component Σ of odd Euler characteristic has [α̃]₀|_Σ = 0, and a = [α̃]₁ + w₁(Σ) on Σ, [α̃]₁ elsewhere.
deg(a ∪ w₁) = 0, so a = cl_R(θ) (PI.9/enriques-picard-image); subtracting θ gives a lift whose first component vanishes on Θ, and PI.7/unramified-odd-or-vanishing gives index 2.

nodes.title: The field of real Puiseux series
nodes.statement: K = ⋃_{n ≥ 1} ℝ((t^{1/n})), the union along the inclusions ℝ((t^{1/n})) ⊂ ℝ((t^{1/m})) for n | m; equivalently the subfield of Hahn series ℝ((t^ℚ)) whose support is contained in (1/n)ℤ and bounded below for some n. It is a real closed field (IsRealClosed K) in which t is positive and infinitesimal; it is non-archimedean. Semialgebraic topology and cohomology over K are those of AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.6.
hypotheses: Ordering: the sign of the leading coefficient.
proofSteps: Define K inside Mathlib's HahnSeries ℚ ℝ as the union over n of the image of the Laurent series in t^{1/n} (support in (1/n)ℤ, well ordered and bounded below).

Real closedness: K(√−1) = ⋃ ℂ((t^{1/n})) is algebraically closed (Newton–Puiseux), and K is ordered by leading coefficients, so K is real closed (Mathlib's isRealClosed from an algebraically closed quadratic extension, via upstream RealAlgebraicGeometry Layer 1).
0 < t < r for every real r > 0, so K is non-archimedean.
acceptance: t^{1/2} ∈ K is a square root of t.
The polynomial X² − t has two roots in K.

nodes.title: The sextic double plane and its K3 resolution
nodes.statement: Over ℝ[[t]] let 𝒳 = {z² = (w² − u² − v²)u²v² − t w⁶}, a double cover of ℙ² branched along a sextic. Its base change to K = RealPuiseux has rational double points only, and the minimal resolution S of 𝒳_K is a K3 surface over K (smooth projective geometrically connected with K_S ≅ O_S and H¹(O_S) = 0). S(K) has four semialgebraically connected components, distinguished by the signs of u/w and v/w, each semialgebraically homeomorphic to a sphere, so H¹(S(K), 𝔽₂) = 0 (semialgebraic cohomology).
hypotheses: Verify the K3 property from the equation (double plane branched along a sextic with ADE singularities), not from an unaccepted K3 roadmap.
proofSteps: The branch sextic f = (w² − u² − v²)u²v² − tw⁶ has only ADE singularities over K (for t ≠ 0 the components separate), so the double cover has rational double points and its minimal resolution has trivial canonical bundle and q = 0.

Real points: z² = f requires f ≥ 0; BCR Example 15.2.2 shows the semialgebraic set {f ≥ 0} in the affine chart w = 1 has four bounded components, one in each sign quadrant of (u, v), and the double cover over each is a sphere.
Semialgebraic cohomology of a semialgebraic sphere vanishes in degree 1 (AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.6).
acceptance: At t = 0 the special fibre is the double cover z² = (w² − u² − v²)u²v², whose normalisation is the quadric z² = w² − u² − v².

nodes.title: The class is not a quaternion class
nodes.statement: The class α of PI.9/prescribed-evaluation-class has index ≠ 2, hence index 4.
hypotheses: Generic-point form of the source's sign argument (RealSurfacePeriodIndex/E13).
proofSteps: If α = (f, g) with f, g ∈ K(S)ˣ, then at points x outside zeros and poles, x ∈ Ξ iff f(x) > 0 or g(x) > 0.

Descend f, g to ℝ((t^{1/n})) and multiply by suitable powers of the positive t^{1/n} (preserving signs) so that they specialise to nonzero rational functions f₀, g₀ on the special fibre, viewed on the quadric Q = {z² = w² − u² − v²}.

On the divisor D = {u = 0} ⊂ Q, choose general real points on the arc v/w < 0, avoiding zeros and poles of the unit parts of f₀, g₀ after factoring the powers of u; the sign pattern there forces even orders of f₀, g₀ along D.
At general points of the arc v/w > 0, the signs of f₀, g₀ are then constant across D, contradicting the required jump between u/w > 0 (in Ξ) and u/w < 0 (not in Ξ).
ind(α) divides 4 by PI.1/real-closed-norm-bound (de Jong over K(√−1)), and is not 2, so it is 4.
acceptance: The index of α is 4 while its period is 2.

gaps.title: Propositions 4.4, 4.5 and 6.6 for nonconstant real evaluation on Ψ
gaps.detail: The printed proofs need [α̃]₀ = 1 on Ψ. When Ψ ⊃ Θ contains components where α evaluates to 0, the Picard correction would have to have real class 1_Θ·[e]₁ on Ψ, which need not be algebraic. The main theorems use only the uniform case (constant [α̃]₀ = t on Ψ), proved in PI.4/uniform-obstruction-vanishing, PI.4/uniform-pushforward-adjustment and PI.6/degree-two-splitting-uniform. The general statements remain open.

gaps.title: De Jong's reduction to unramified classes and the Lefschetz principle
gaps.detail: PI.1/de-jong-period-index rests on two cited inputs that no layer of the atlas plans: the transfer of the index of a class over k(S) along an extension of algebraically closed base fields of characteristic 0 (Lefschetz principle with index base-change invariance), and de Jong 2004 §7, which reduces a ramified class on a complex surface to an unramified one on another model without changing period or index. The unramified complex case is planned in PI.2. Both inputs are needed for every theorem that invokes de Jong (odd periods, the norm bound, Enriques period four, the Puiseux example).

gaps.title: Relative pair transport in the final deformation step
gaps.detail: PI.6/kummer-lift-transport needs either an equivariant stratified trivialisation of the pair (𝒯, p⁻¹R) over a small real parameter neighbourhood, with invariant Whitney stratification containing the fixed exceptional curves over Sing R and the moving ℙ¹ fibres over R ∩ D and invariant control data (the hypotheses of AlgebraicTopologyPartII:AT2.16/stratified-pair-transport), or a direct ambient cohomological transport of the restriction to T_U. Neither has been verified for this family (extraction gap G13).

gaps.title: Signed homological comparison of the double-cover chase (inherited)

gaps.title: Cited real-algebraic inputs not reconstructed
gaps.detail: Three cited theorems are used as stated, with no atlas owner and no reconstructed proof: Bröcker 1980 Satz a), b) (PI.6/brocker-sign-input), Mangolte–van Hamel 1998 Theorem 4.4 on the real Picard image of Enriques surfaces (PI.9/enriques-picard-image), and Colliot-Thélène–Parimala 1990 Proposition 3.1.2 on realising evaluation functions (PI.9/prescribed-evaluation-class). gaps.title: Classical quadratic-form inputs cited through secondary sources
gaps.detail: Albert's theorem on biquaternion algebras (PI.0/albert-isotropy, cited from Lam's book, not read), the Elman–Lam analysis of fields with u(F(√−1)) ≤ 4 (PI.0/elman-lam-c2-bound, stated by Becher 2005 §3 for u(F(√−1)) = 4 with reference to Elman–Lam 1973, not read; the case u(F(√−1)) < 4 is taken from Elman–Lam without a checked locator), and the anticanonical model of a degree-four del Pezzo surface as an intersection of two quadrics (PI.7/del-pezzo-point, cited, not read) are used as stated.
